ARTICLE I.  IN GENERAL
Sec.  2-1.  Officers to turn receipts over to finance director.

Unless  otherwise  specifically  provided  by  law,  all fees and other monies received by any officer or employee of the city in the city's behalf shall be promptly paid over to the director of finance.
Sec.  2-2.  Manager to appoint boards and commissions secretaries.

Except  as  otherwise  provided  by  this  Code  with reference  to  particular  boards  and  commissions,  the city manager shall appoint and designate secretaries of boards and commissions of the city.
Sec.  2-3.  Copies of official documents.

Except as otherwise provided, copies of any official document may be obtained from the city clerk for a charge fifteen cents ($0.15) per page; except that this charge shall not be assessed against city officers, board or agency members.
Sec.  2-3.1.  National criminal history screening for city manager.
(a)  Pursuant  to  F .S.  §  166.0442,  as  such  may  be amended from time to time, state and national criminal history  background  checks  shall  be  required  for  the city manager.

(b)  Each such person shall be fingerprinted who is applying for city manager or continuing employment or appointment as city manager. The city department of  human  resources,  its  successor  department,  and other applicable departments shall conduct such state and national criminal history background checks.

(c)  Fingerprints obtained pursuant to the authority of  this section shall be submitted to the state department of  law enforcement for a state criminal history records check and also to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for a national criminal history records check. The information obtained from each respective criminal  history  record  check  conducted  pursuant  to  this section shall be used to determine a person's eligibility
Supp. No. 1
for  employment or appointment and to determine a person's eligibility for continued employment and appointment.
Sec.  2-4.  Notary fee.

In addition to any other fees or charges prescribed or required by this Code, any other ordinance, or by law, there shall be a charge of one dollar and fifty cents ($1.50) for the notarizing of any document by any city officer or employee, except that this charge shall not be assessed against city officers, board or agency members.
Sec.  2-5.  Approval  required  to  use  community  buildings, facilities; application.

The use of community buildings, or other facilities of  the city shall be permitted by individuals, civic or other quasi-public organizations without commercial purpose as permitted by the manager without rent or other payment. Individuals, firms or corporations may use buildings or facilities designated by the manager for commercial purposes for such rent as may be determined by the city manager and approved by the city commission. The following are minimum requirements in addition to such other requirements as may be requested by the city manager:
(a) Written application must be made to the city manager and if by an organization, attested by its secretary, for the use of  the facilities on a specific date.
(b) The  application  shall  state  the  purpose  for which the building or other facilities are to be used,  whether  or  not  admission  fees  or  any other charges are to be made.
Sec.  2-6.  Responsibility for damages arising from use of community buildings or facilities.
The person or organization using community buildings or other facilities shall be responsible for any and all  damages  that  might  occur  during  the  use  of  the
OPA-LOCKA CODE
premises, either to the premises or to a person using the same and, in addition to all other requirements provided in this Code, such person or organization shall:
(1) Indemnify  and  hold  harmless  the  city  from any and all liability whatsoever in the use of the buildings by any such person or organization;

(2) Provide  a  performance  bond  in  an  amount established  by  the  city  manager  conditioned on restoring the premises to the same condition  as  existed  prior  to  use  and  for  faithful performance  of  all  regulatory  provisions  of this Code applicable to use of  buildings and facilities.
Sec.  2-7.  Regulations governing use of community buildings and facilities.
The use of  the buildings or other facilities shall be subject to the following regulations:

(a) The city manager or his designee will open up the building for the use of  the buildings, but the applicant is responsible for extinguishing lights and locking up the building and placing furniture and equipment back in place as found.
(b) No bicycle, roller skates or other vehicles will be allowed in any public building.
(c) Except as provided in F.S. § 413.08, no dogs or other animals are allowed on the premises.
(d) The applicant assumes full responsibility for the proper use of  city furnishings and other facilities.
(e) No applications will be accepted from minors except through a responsible chaperone.
(f) No improper, illegal or offensive use shall be permitted.
Sec.  2-8.  Procedures for organizations, agencies requesting assistance from city.
(a)  All organizations, agencies or governmental entities  requesting monies or other assistance from the city for purposes beneficial to the citizens of  the city
Supp. No. 1
shall, prior to making application for said request to the city commission, submit to the city manager the following:

(1) A true copy of the charter, bylaws, governmental authority, federal tax-exempt number and other information setting forth the nature of the organization, agency or governmental entity making the request.
(2) A statement as to the nature of the request and the  beneficial  services  to  be  supplied  to  the citizens of the city.

(3) Fiscal information relating to the amount of the request, the current financial statement of the applicant, the amount of said monies to be expended within the city limits or for the benefit of the citizens of the city.

(4) A statement  showing  all  sources  of  revenue during the past two (2) years for the project, including the total amount of  support from other jurisdictions, whether fiscal, in kind or through use of tax exemption or other indirect support.
(5) The names, addresses and qualifications of all directors, officers and agents of the organization, agency or governmental entity.
(6) The city manager may require such additional information or exhibits as may be necessary to inform  the  city  commission  as  to  the  valid public purpose to be served by said request.
(b)  All applications for support from the city, whether fiscal or in kind, shall be filed with the city manager no later than the first Tuesday of  June of  each calendar year.

(c)  The city manager shall, prior to the preparation of  the annual budget, submit all applications for support to the city commission for consideration. Those organizations, agencies or governmental entities receiving  approval  from  the  city  commission  for  support shall be included in the annual budget of  the city in such amounts as may be authorized by the city commission.
ADMINISTRATION
Sec.  2-8.1.  Defense of civil actions against public officers, employees or agents.

The policy of  the city is to provide an attorney to defend any civil action arising from a complaint for damages or injury suffered as a result of  any act or omission  of  action  of  any  of  its  officers  or  former officers, employees or former employees, or agents for an act or omission arising out of and in the scope of his or her employment or function, unless, in the case of a tort action, the officer, employee, or agent acted in bad faith, with malicious purpose, or in a manner exhibiting  wanton  and  willful  disregard  of  human  rights, safety, or property.
Sec.  2-8.2.  Payment of judgments or settlements against certain public officers or employees.
(1)  The city shall expend available funds to pay:

(a) Any final judgment, including damages, costs, and attorney fees, arising from a complaint for damages or injury suffered as a result of  any act  or  omission  of  action  of  any  officer  or employee in a civil or civil rights lawsuit described  in  F .S.  §  111.07.  If  the  civil  action arises under F.S. § 768.28 as a tort claim, the limitations and provisions of F.S. § 768.28 governing payment shall apply. If  the action is a civil rights action arising under 42 USC 1983, or  similar  federal  statutes,  payments  for  the full  amount  of  the  judgment  may  be  made unless the officer, employee, or agent has been determined in the final judgment to have caused the harm intentionally.
(b) Any compromise or settlement of any claim or litigation as described in subsection (a) of this section, subject to the limitations set forth in subsection (a) of this section.
(c) Any reimbursement required under F .S. § 111.07 for  court  costs  and  reasonable  attorney  fees when the city has failed to provide an attorney and the defendant prevails.
(2)  For the purpose of this section, the term "final judgment" means a judgment upon completion of any appellate proceedings.
Supp. No. 1
Sec.  2-8.3.  Provision  of  insurance  in  anticipation  of judgments  or  settlements  against  officers, employees or agents of the city.

The  city  manager,  on  behalf  of  the  city  and  its employees and officers, is authorized to enter into risk management programs, or to purchase liability insurance for whatever coverage it may choose or to have any combination thereof  in anticipation of  any judgment  or  settlement  which  its  officers,  employees,  or agents may be liable to pay pursuant to a civil or civil rights lawsuit described in F.S. § 111.07.
Sec.  2-8.4.  Search committee established as option.

(a)  There may be established a five-member search committee for the purpose of soliciting, screening and recommending,  when  applicable,  candidates  for  the positions of city manager, city attorney and city clerk.

(b)  The committee shall mean the city commission, or  any  other  such  committee  appointed  by  the  city commission to solicit, screen and recommend candidates for the positions of  city manager, city attorney and city clerk. The committee shall elect a chairperson and determine its meeting dates and times. The committee shall notice and conduct its meetings in accordance with the city's Charter and Code, and applicable federal,  state  and  local  laws.  If  the  city  commission decides to appoint a search committee, other than itself to serve, the names of the appointees of the mayor and each commissioner shall be submitted to the city clerk not later than ten (10) days of  the position becoming vacant.

(c)  If  a search is conducted, the search committee shall  make  every  effort  to  conduct  a  thorough  local and/or nationwide search for candidates for the positions of city manager, city attorney and city clerk.

(d)  In conducting its search for candidates, the committee shall use, at a minimum, the qualifications for the positions contained in articles I, III and V, respectively, of the city Charter as the criteria for evaluating each candidate.
(e)  The  committee  shall  convene  and  conduct  its search and make a recommendation, if  applicable, of no more than five (5) candidates for the vacant position.
OPA-LOCKA CODE
(f)  The search committee shall dissolve automatically upon the appointment by the city commission of a candidate to the vacant position.

(g)  Nothing set forth in this section shall be prevent the city commission from directly appointing a candidate by a majority vote of the city commission for the positions of city manager, city clerk and city attorney. (Code 1983, § 2-8.4; Ord. No. 02-6, §§ 2-7, 4-10-2002; Ord. No. 09-15, § 2, 9-9-2009; Ord. No. 2025-18, § 2, 6-23-2025)
Sec.  2-8.5.  Notification of funding sources by community-based organizations.

All  community-based  organizations  shall  be  required to notify the city manager by letter on October 1,  annually,  its  source  of  funding  (federal,  state,  or county), including the amount thereof and the nature and scope of services to be rendered to the community. (Code 1983, § 2-8.5; Ord. No. 08-01, § 2, 1-9-2008)

Sec.  2-9.  Applicability and definitions.

(a)  Unless otherwise indicated, this article shall be applicable to and binding upon every officer, official and employee of  the city, including every member of any board, commission or agency of the city, including those normally considered autonomous and/or semiautonomous.  Other  than  the  city  attorney,  this article shall not be applicable to attorneys who represent the city, either in a ceremonial or other capacity.
(b)  References in this article to the Florida Statutes (F.S.) shall be interpreted as meaning state statutes, as amended from time to time.
Business entity shall have the meaning ascribed in F.S. § 112.312(5).
Candidate shall have the meaning ascribed in F.S. § 112.312(6).
Conflict or conflict of interest shall have the meaning ascribed in F.S. § 112.312(8).
Gift shall have  the meaning  ascribed  in  F.S. § 112.312(12).

Sec.  2-10.  Transacting  business  with  city;  appearing before  city  commission,  agencies  and/or boards.

(a)  No  person  included  in  section  2-9  shall  enter into any contract or transact any business with the city or any person or agency acting for the city. Nor shall such person appear in representation of any third party before the city commission or other city board, commission or agency. Any such contract, agreement or appearance  entered  into  in  violation  of  this  section shall render any transaction resulting from the same voidable.

(b)  The term "person" appearing in subsection (a) of  this section shall, for purposes of  this section, include officers, officials and employees, as set forth in section 2-9, and the following family members of such person: spouse, son, daughter, parent, brother or sister.

(c)  The prohibition upon any activity which is set forth in subsection (a) of  this section shall remain in effect  for  a  period  of  two  (2)  years  after  the  officer, official, or employee has left city service or terminated city employment.
Sec.  2-11.  Applicability of F.S. ch. 112.

Nothing in the city code of ethics for public officers shall  be  interpreted  or  construed  as  conflicting  with F.S. ch. 112, pt. III (F .S. § 112.311 et seq.), which is also applicable to public officers of  the city. This article is intended to supplement state law provisions governing ethics in government.

Sec.  2-13.  Standards of conduct.

In furtherance of the public trust assumed by public officers of the city upon their election or appointment to  public  office  or  employment,  the  following  standards of conduct shall be applicable to public officers of the city:
(a) Core values . Each public officer pledges his or her commitment to the core values of the city, as follows:
(1) Leadership by example. A public officer will display leadership by:
a. Subscribing to the city's ethics for public officers;
b. Promoting a sense of community, community  values,  and  community spirit and by embracing diversity  within  the  community,  while focusing  on  the  importance  and values of family;
c. Practicing a "can do" attitude rather than an attitude of negativity and division;
d. Developing vision or focus on the future, and supporting the achievement of vision;
e. Being responsive;
f. Having fun and enjoying one's role as a public officer of the city;
g. Recognizing and fostering leadership  throughout  the  city  government and the residential and business communities of the city;
h. Balancing statesmanship and political and professional goals;
i. Maintaining a positive image, while working towards the best interests of the city and its citizens; and
j. Treat  everyone  with  respect  and courtesy, even during times when there is disagreement.
(2) Empowerment (mindset/orientation) attitude. A public  officer  will  display  an empowerment attitude by:
a. Encouraging citizens to be active, responsible partners in city government that function with public officers of the city to achieve a shared vision;
b. Empowering city administration to continuously  improve  the  quality of  and  the  services  provided  by city government;
c. Encouraging entrepreneurship by governing the city as a successful, ethical business model; and
d. Maximizing revenue for the city.
(3) Customer focus and involvement (volunteerism/action). A  public  officer will  encourage  and  promote  customer focus and involvement by:
a. Encouraging citizens and residents to be involved in government and bridging the gap between city government and community;
b. Promoting  specific avenues by which citizen input is gathered and information is disseminated by the city;
c. Encouraging citizen involvement in decision-making; and
d. Supporting  data-based  decisionmaking.

(4) Continuous improvement. A public officer  will  work  towards  continuous  improvement through:
a. Self-improvement through education,  personal  growth,  and  personal learning;
b. Supporting  process  improvement in city systems and key process improvements  through  knowledgebased decision-making;
c. Supporting and encouraging personal wellness and professional development throughout city government;
d. Supporting  innovation  through technology; and
e. Promoting  effective  use  of  customer feedback to improve quality of  government and the providing of government services.

(b) Each public officer shall be dedicated to the concepts of effective and democratic local government, respecting the principals and spirit of representative democracy, and setting a positive example of  good citizenship by scrupulously observing the letter and spirit of applicable laws, rules, and regulations.

(c) Each  public  officer  shall  pledge  himself  or herself to affirm the dignity and worth of the services rendered by city government and to maintain a constructive, creative, and practical attitude towards urban affairs incorporating a deep sense of  social responsibility as a public servant.

(d) Each public officer shall be dedicated to the highest  ideals  of  honor  and  integrity  in  all public  and  personal  relationships  and  shall conduct themselves in a manner which maintains and promotes public confidence in city government.
(e) Each  public  officer  shall  recognize  that  the main function of local government, at all times, is to serve and promote the best interests of the public.
(f) Each public officer pledges to keep the community informed on the affairs of city government,  emphasize  and  practice  friendly  and

courteous service  to  the  public,  and  seek  to improve the quality and image of  public service.

(h) Each public officer pledges not to improperly influence or attempt to influence other public officers.

(i) A public  officer  shall  not  engage  in,  solicit, negotiate for, or promise to accept private employment or render services for private interests or conduct a private business when such employment, service, or business creates a conflict  with  the  proper  discharge  of  his  or  her official duties as a public officer.

No ordinance, resolution or motion shall be adopted by the commission without the affirmative vote of the majority of all the members. Any member of the commission who announces a conflict of  interest on a particular matter and a decision to refrain from voting or otherwise  participating  in  the  proceedings  related  to  that matter shall leave the commission chambers until the consideration of  that matter is concluded. Any such member  who  does  not  leave  the  chambers  shall  be deemed absent for purposes of constituting a quorum, counting the vote, or for any other purpose.

(b)  Should  no  quorum  attend  within  thirty  (30) minutes after the hour appointed for the meeting of the commission, the mayor, or the vice-mayor or, in their absence,  the  clerk  or  his  designee,  may  adjourn  the meeting until the next day, unless by unanimous agree-
OPA-LOCKA CODE

ment another day and time shall be established by those members present and their action at such meeting shall be recorded in the minutes by the clerk. (Code 1955, § 2-8; Code 1983, § 2-51; Ord. No. 81-3, § 1,
Sec.  2-52.  Order of business.

All meetings of the commission shall be open to the public. Promptly at the hour set for each meeting, the members of the commission, the city attorney, the city manager  and  the  city  clerk  shall  take  their  regular chairs in the commission chamber, and the business of the commission shall be taken up for consideration and disposition in accordance with the agenda for the meeting.
Sec.  2-53.  Rules of debate.

(a) Question under consideration. When a motion is presented and seconded, it is under consideration and no other motion shall be received thereafter, except to adjourn, to lay on the table, to postpone, or to amend until the question is decided. These motions shall have preference in the order in which they are mentioned and the first two (2) shall be decided without debate. Final action upon a pending motion may be deferred until  a  date  certain  by  a  majority  of  the  members present.

(b) As to the chairman. Upon relinquishing the chair, the mayor or such other member of the commission, as may be presiding, may move, second and debate, subject only to such limitations of  debate as are by these rules imposed upon all members.

(c) Getting the floor, improper references to be avoided. Every member desiring to speak for any purpose shall address  the  presiding  officer,  and,  upon  recognition, shall  confine  himself  to  the  question  under  debate, avoiding all personalities and indecorous language.

(d) Interruption. A member, once recognized, shall not be interrupted when speaking unless it is to call him to order or as otherwise provided. If a member, while speaking,  is  called  to  order,  he  shall  cease  speaking until the question of order is determined by the presiding  officer,  and  if,  in  order,  he  shall  be  permitted  to proceed. Any member may appeal to the commission from the decision of the chair upon a question of order,
Supp. No. 1
when,  without  debate,  the  chair  shall  submit  to  the commission  the  question,  "Shall  the  decision  of  the chair be sustained?" and the commission shall decide by a majority vote.
(e) Privilege  of  closing  debate. The  commissioner moving the adoption of  an ordinance, resolution or motion shall have the privilege of closing the debate.

(f) Roll call. Upon any roll call, there shall be no discussion by any member voting, and he shall vote yes or  no.  Any  member,  upon  voting,  may  give  a  brief statement to explain his vote. A member shall have the privilege of filing with the city clerk a written explanation of his vote. Any member of the commission who announces a conflict of interest on a particular matter and  a  decision  to  refrain  from  voting  or  otherwise participating in the proceedings related to that matter shall leave the commission chambers until the consideration of that matter is concluded. Any such member who  does  not  leave  the  chambers  shall  be  deemed absent for purposes of constituting a quorum, counting the vote, or for any other purpose.
ADMINISTRATION

(g) Reconsideration. An action of  the commission may be reconsidered only at the same meeting at which the action was taken. A motion to reconsider may be made only by a member who voted on the prevailing side of  the question. Adoption of  a motion to reconsider shall rescind the action reconsidered.
(h) Vote change. Any commissioner may change his vote before the next item is called for consideration, or before  a  recess  or  adjournment  is  called  whichever occurs first but not thereafter.

(i) Renewal. Once  action  is  taken  on  a  proposed ordinance,  neither  the  same  matter  nor  its  repeal  or rescission may be brought before the commission again during the six (6) month period following the action (subject  to  the  provisions  of  subsection  (g)  of  this section),  unless  application  for  renewal  by  four  (4) members of  the commission is first submitted to the mayor. Should an ordinance be proposed that raises the  same  previously  resolved  matter,  or  its  repeal  or rescission, in different or modified form during the six (6) month period, the mayor may declare the proposal out of order.
Sec.  2-54.  Reading minutes.

Unless  a  reading  of  the  minutes  of  a  meeting  is requested by a majority of the commission, such minutes, when approved by the commission and signed by the mayor and the city clerk, shall be considered approved without reading, provided that the  city  clerk delivers a copy thereof to each member of the commission and to the city attorney at least two (2) full working days preceding the meeting. The minutes of  prior meetings may be approved by a majority of the members present, and upon such approval shall become the official minutes.
Sec.  2-55.  Method of voting.

Upon every roll call, the names of the commissioners  shall  be  called  alphabetically  by  surname,  except that the names shall be rotated after each roll call vote, so that the commissioner who voted first on a preceding roll call shall vote last upon the next subsequent matter; provided, however, that the mayor, if presiding, shall always cast his vote last. Upon relinquishing the

chair, the mayor may vote in alphabetical order with the other commissioners, and the then presiding officer shall  cast  his  vote  last.  The  clerk  shall  call  the  roll, tabulate the votes, and announce the results. The vote upon every ordinance and resolution shall be taken by roll  call.  The  vote  upon  any  motion or other matter may be by voice vote, provided that the chairman or any commissioner may require a roll call vote to be taken upon any resolution or motion if request is made by a commissioner.
Sec.  2-56.  Addressing the commission.

(a) Agenda items. All proceedings and the order of business  at  all  meetings  of  the  commission  shall  be conducted in accordance with the official agenda. Any person  shall  be  entitled  to  be  placed  on  the  official agenda  of  a  regular  meeting  of  the  commission  in accordance herewith. The deadline for placing a person on the agenda is 12:00 noon on Wednesday of the week preceding the week of the meeting at which the person wishes  to  be  heard.  Any  person  shall  be  entitled  to speak on any matter appearing on the official agenda under the sections entitled "public hearings," and "public presentation of matters by citizens," only as to those items listed in the agenda.
(b) Non-agenda matters. Persons shall address the commission  on  non-agenda  matters  only  during  the citizens' forum.
Sec.  2-57.  Addressing commission, manner, time.

(a)  Each  person,  other  than  salaried  members  of the city staff, who address the commission shall step up to the front of  the commission and shall give the following information in an audible tone of voice for the minutes:
(1) Name;
(2) Address;
(3) Whether  he  speaks  for  himself,  a  group  of persons, or a third party. If the person represents an individual or organization, the commission may require the speaker to:
a. Indicate the number of members in the organization;
OPA-LOCKA CODE

b. The date of  the most recent meeting of the  organization's  board  or  governing council, and whether the view expressed by the speaker represents an established policy of  the organization approved by the board or governing council.

(b)  Unless further time is granted by the commission, he shall limit his address to three (3) minutes. All remarks  shall  be  addressed  to  the  commission  as  a body and not to any member thereof. No person, other than commissioners, city manager, city attorney or city clerk and the person having the floor, shall be permitted to enter into any discussion, either directly or through a  member of  the commission, without the presiding officer.  No  question  shall  be  asked  a  commissioner except through a presiding officer.
Sec.  2-58.  Decorum.
The city commission desires to exercise the following standards for decorum:

(a) Any person making impertinent or slanderous remarks or who becomes boisterous while addressing the commission, shall be declared to be out of order by the presiding officer, unless permission to continue or again address the commission be granted by the majority vote of the commission members present.

(b) Ground rules for decorum regarding members of  the  city  commission.  The  following  shall constitute  the  guidelines  for  decorum  to  be adhered to by members of  the city commission in their respective roles as elected public officers of the city:
(1) Members of the city commission shall:
a. Each conduct themselves with dignity;
b. Agree to disagree with each other; and
c. Show respect for the points of view of other members of the city commission.
(2) Members of  the city commission shall not:
a. Falsely accuse another member of the city commission of  wrongdoing;
b. Criticize each other in a rancorous or unprofessional manner;
c. Make personal attacks on another member of the city commission; or
d. Individually act without the support of the city commission.
(3) Members of the city commission in treatment toward appointed officers and generally city staff shall:
a. Make all efforts to meet with staff and appointed officers in advance of public meetings on issues of concern to the commissioner;
b. Work  with  appointed  officers  to make sound decisions for the city;
c. Treat appointed officers and staff with  courtesy  and  respect  during public meetings;
d. Refrain from suggesting that staff is  being  dishonest  or  otherwise speaking in a manner that would cause clear embarrassment to staff during public meetings.
Sec.  2-59.  Sergeant-at-arms.

The police chief, or such other city official or employee as the commission may designate, shall be the sergeant-at-arms of the commission meeting. The sergeant-at-arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding officer for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the meetings. (Code 1955, § 2-8; Code 1983, § 2-59; Ord. No. 81-3, § 1,
Sec.  2-60.  Committees.

(a)  There shall be no committee of the board of city commissioners, other than those provided for in subsection (b) of  this section, except that the board may resolve  itself  into  a  committee  of  the  whole  at  any regular  or  special  meeting  and  select  a  chairman  to preside  over  such  meeting  of  the  committee  of  the whole. Provided, however, that all committees in being at the time of the adoption of these rules shall continue
ADMINISTRATION
in existence until dissolved by vote of a majority of the commission members present at any regular meeting, or at a special meeting called for that purpose.

In addition thereto, whenever the commission deems it necessary or desirable that the commission shall be  represented  at  meetings,  conferences  or  other occasions involving other governmental entities, agencies, officials or groups, or nongovernmental organizations,  or  departments,  agencies  or  officials  of the city government, the mayor, or the vice mayor in his absence may designate members of the commission or himself to represent the commission at such meetings, conferences or other occasions, with the consent of  the designee. A majority of  the board then present may disapprove any such appointment. Such representatives shall have no power to act for or  on  behalf  of  the  commission  or  to  make  any commitment or binding obligation on behalf of the commission of  the city. Such representatives shall report in writing to the commission with regard to such meeting, conference or other occasion.

(b)  The  commission may establish special ad hoc committees from time to time as specific needs arise. The mayor, or vice-mayor in his absence, shall make appointments to such committees with the consent of the appointees. A majority of the commission present may disapprove any appointment. Any special ad hoc committee may be abolished by the mayor, or the vicemayor in his absence, when its continued existence no longer is necessary. A majority of the board then present may disapprove any such action.
Sec.  2-61.  Ordinances, resolutions, motions, contracts.

(a) Preparation of ordinances. The city attorney, when requested,  shall  prepare  ordinances  and  resolutions. Ordinances  may  be  introduced  and  adopted  by  title and shall be read by title only by the city attorney or his designed before consideration by the commission on first reading. Copies of  all proposed ordinances shall be furnished to each commissioner and shall be made available to all interested persons.

(b) Introducing for passage or approval. Ordinances, resolution  and  other  matters  and  subjects  requiring action  by  the  commission,  must  be  introduced  and sponsored by a member of the commission, except that either the city manager or the city attorney may present

ordinances, resolutions and other matters or subjects to the commission for consideration, and any commissioner may assume sponsorship thereof by moving that such  ordinance,  resolution,  matter  or  subject  be  adopted in accordance with law; otherwise they shall not be considered.

(c) When action to be taken by resolution or ordinance. All actions of the commission may be taken by resolution or ordinance except that any action of  the commission which provides for raising revenue, appropriating funds or incurring indebtedness, or which provide a penalty or establishes a rule or regulation for the violation of  which a penalty is imposed, shall be by ordinance, and except that approval of purely administrative matters may be accomplished by motion duly adopted and recorded in the minutes of  the meeting. Whenever action cannot be taken because the vote of the commission has resulted in a tie, the status quo shall continue in effect and the proposed ordinance, resolution  or  motion  that  produced  the  tie  vote  shall  be removed from the agenda without prejudice to its reintroduction on a de novo basis at a later time.
Sec.  2-62.  Adjournment.
A motion to adjourn shall always be in order and decided without debate. (Code 1955, § 2-8; Code 1983, § 2-62; Ord. No. 81-3, § 1, 1-14-1981)
Sec.  2-63.  Clerk, minutes, agenda.

The city clerk, or his designated deputy clerk, shall act  as  clerk  of  the  commission.  The  city  clerk  shall duplicate  the  minutes  and  all  resolutions  and  ordinances, and for a reasonable charge shall furnish copies to  persons  desiring  them.  The  city  clerk  shall  make available to the commissioners a copy of  the agenda seventy-two (72) hours before the meeting.
Sec.  2-64.  Suspension of the rules.
No rule of  procedure adopted by this commission shall be suspended. (Code 1955, § 2-8; Code 1983, § 2-64; Ord. No. 81-3, § 1,
OPA-LOCKA CODE
Sec.  2-65.  State of the city.
The mayor shall prepare and deliver a report on the state  of  the  city  to  the  people  of  the  city  between January 1 and January 31, annually. Such report shall
be prepared after consultation with city commissioners, city manager and the city attorney. (Code 1955, § 2-8; Code 1983, § 2-65; Ord. No. 81-3, § 1, 1-14-1981)
Sec.  2-66.  Appeal procedure before commission.

Unless otherwise provided by Charter or ordinance, or the provisions of the zoning and land development regulations, any person may appeal any administrative action to the city commission by giving notice of  appeal within the appeal period provided by ordinance, or in the event no appeal period is provided by ordinance within  thirty  (30)  days  after  the  final  administrative action by filing with the city clerk a notice of  appeal stating the following:
(1) The full name and address of the appellant;
(2) The  date  of  the  final  administrative  action appealed from;
(3) The  nature  of  the  administrative  action  appealed from;
(4) Whether or not the person is represented by an attorney or any other person and, if  so, the name and address of  the attorney or person representing the appellant;
Sec.  2-67.  Residents' right to know.

(a) Legislative intent. It  shall  be  the  policy of  the city  to  provide  targeted  neighborhood  notice,  timely opportunities for input, and procedural fairness in hearings  for  any  proposed  policy,  ordinance,  project,  or other matter that impacts residents' quality of life.
(b) Impacts to residents' quality of life. Matters that impact residents' quality of life shall include the following:
(1) Any position that has been formally adopted by  resolution  of  a  registered  neighborhood association and transmitted to the city through its city manager;

(2) Any application  for  development  review  before the city's land use boards, or any proposed zoning legislation before the city commission that includes the potential for lot aggregation or that includes the potential for material increase in traffic over current levels; required parking; building height; base elevation; intensity of uses; density, or floor area ratio;
(3) Development proposals that require approval by the city commission which propose:
a. Changes of use or commercialization in a  public  park,  public  beach,  or  other public property or public easement;
b. The  design  and  implementation  of  a streetscape, transit, pedestrian parking, or area improvement project (other than routine repairs and maintenance); and
(4) Any  material  change  to  any  of  the  matters listed in subsections (b)(1) through (3) of this section.

For  purposes  of  this  section,  the  term  "material  increase" means any increase in building height or base elevation over three (3) feet, any increase in density, or any increase in floor area ratio. Additionally, the term "material increase" means any increase in traffic over current  levels,  required  parking,  or  intensity  of  uses that the planning director considers to be substantial.

(c) Targeted neighborhood notice. The city commission  shall  adopt  a  process  by  resolution  (as  may  be amended from time to time) for registering neighborhood associations and shall provide targeted electronic notices on matters that impact residents' quality of life, as defined above, and, in addition to targeted electronic notice,  the  city  shall  post  such  notices  on  the  city's website. Targeted neighborhood notices at each step in the public process, excluding emergency matters requiring immediate action, shall be in addition to any other public notices required by law. Notices shall be written in plain English, and both the title and summary shall objectively describe the proposed action.

For purposes of this section, the term "neighborhood association" means an organization of residential homeowners and tenants created to address quality  of life  issues  in  a  defined  neighborhood  or community.
Notwithstanding  the  above,  an  individual  resident of  Opa-locka may also register to receive tar-
ADMINISTRATION

geted neighborhood notices. In order to be eligible for registration, an individual shall have been a resident of  the city for a minimum of  six (6) months and must provide the city with a reasonable form of identification exhibiting proof  of  residency (to be defined in the resolution described above) upon registering.
Registered neighborhood associations (and individuals  who  choose  to  register)  must  renew  their registrations on an annual basis.

(d) Timely  opportunities  for  input. Once  a  matter that impacts residents' quality of life (as defined in this section) is referred to a city commission committee or land use board, or once a matter is placed on an agenda for approval by the city commission, the city shall use reasonable good faith efforts to ensure that registered neighborhood associations (and individuals who choose to register) have an opportunity to participate in city processes that shape any matter that impacts residents' quality  of  life  (as  defined  in  subsection  (b)  of  this section).

(e) Procedural fairness in quasi-judicial hearings. The city shall ensure that representatives of registered neighborhood associations (and individuals who choose to register)  shall  have  the  opportunity  at  quasi-judicial hearings before the city's land use boards, or the city commission, to present or rebut evidence relevant to matters that impact residents' quality of life. This shall include the opportunity to request a time certain for the convenience  of  the  public.  Registered  neighborhood associations (and individuals who choose to register) do not need to retain legal counsel to exercise these procedural rights. Notices of filing, and a copy of each quasi-judicial application, shall promptly be made available on the city's website upon filing, and amendments thereto or supplemental information shall be filed and promptly made available on the city's website in advance of the date of the scheduled hearing.

(f) Deferral or reconsideration. A registered neighborhood  association  (or  individual  who  chooses  to register)  may  request  deferral  of  any  matter  that  requires targeted notice, or the reconsideration of  that matter, if  such matter is not duly noticed pursuant to this section. Reconsideration may only be requested at the publicly noticed land use board or city commission meeting immediately following the meeting at which the challenged action was taken. However, the land use board or city commission shall have the sole discretion
to  grant  or  deny  any  such  request.  Consistent  with Robert's Rules of Order, a motion to reconsider must be  made  by  a  board  member  or  commissioner  who voted with the prevailing side.
(g) Amendment or repealer. Any amendment to this section (including the repealer of any provision herein) shall require the affirmative vote of  four-fifths ( ✦ ) of the city commission.

(h) Periodic review and annual report. The city manager,  or  the  city  manager's  designee,  shall,  annually during the city commission's review and approval of the  city's  annual  operating  budget,  present  a  written report to the city commission tracking and identifying the  operational  implementation and fiscal impact of this section. The report shall include statistics relating to the number of registered neighborhood associations and individuals registered under the section and any amendments thereto; issues pertaining to impacts to residents' quality of  life that have resulted in the issuance  of  targeted  notices;  and  any  violations  and/or complaints  received  by  the  city  administration  with regard  to  the  implementation  of  the  procedures  set forth in the section.
(i) Administration of this section. This section shall be administered by the office of the city manager. (Code 1983, § 2-67; Ord. No. 17-16, § 1, 10-25-2017)

ARTICLE III.  ADMINISTRATIVE RULES AND PROCEDURES
DIVISION 1.  GENERALLY
Sec.  2-82.  Applicability generally.

All boards, authorities, committees, officers and agencies of  the city, hereinafter referred to as a board or agency, shall be governed by the following rules, regulations  and  procedures,  except  where  specific  provisions of this Code, establish conflicting provisions, or except as otherwise provided in this article.
OPA-LOCKA CODE
Sec.  2-83.  Special rules or procedures for specific agencies.

In  the  event  any  board  or  agency  of  the  city,  by virtue of its designated function, requires a special rule or administrative procedure, not encompassed within this article, the board or agency may adopt an administrative rule or procedure relating solely to said board or agency, provided the administrative rule or procedure  is  not  inconsistent  with  the  provisions  of  this chapter  and  has  been  passed  by  a  majority  of  the members of said board or agency, or approved by the city manager if promulgated by an administrative officer or department, and shall have been certified to the city commission on the following form:
"CERTIFICATION OF
ADMINISTRATIVE RULE
FILED WITH THE CITY
COMMISSION OF THE
CITY OF OPA-LOCKA, FLORIDA
1. The rule or administrative procedure set forth herein shall be hereafter known as Rule No. of the (board or agency), and is attached hereto.
2. The  purpose  of  adopting  or  amending  said rule or administrative procedure is as follows:
I DO HEREBY CERTIFY that the attached rule or administrative procedure is a true and correct copy as promulgated and adopted on the day of
(Board or Agency)
No. of copies
Certified
Signature of Presiding Officer or City Manager

Each rule or administrative procedure shall be typed on eight and one-half  (8 ½) inches by eleven (11) inches paper, double-spaced, with a two (2) inch margin at the top and bottom, and a one (1) inch margin on either

side. The rule or administrative procedure as filed with the  city  commission  shall  become  effective  after  its approval  by  the  city  commission  by  resolution  duly adopted after public hearing thereon. The city commission shall and does hereby reserve unto itself, the authority to amend, change, alter or nullify any and all rules or procedures established or created by any board or agency of the city at any time.
Sec.  2-84.  Board, agency members to be residents.
All members of any board or agency of the city shall be residents of  the city,  except  where  otherwise provided by this Code or the Charter.
Sec.  2-85.  Family members not to serve on same board or agency.

No two (2) members of  an immediate family shall serve at any one (1) time on any board or agency of the city. Immediate family shall consist of  husband, wife and children. Members of the same immediate family may be appointed to and serve on other boards and agencies of the city.
Sec.  2-86.  Meetings of boards, agencies.

(a) Regular meetings. Regular meetings of any board, authority, committee or agency of the city, except where otherwise provided in this Code, shall begin at a specific time, and on a designated day of  each month as may be designated by a majority of the members of the board or agency and approved by the city commission as  an  administrative  rule  or  procedure  pursuant  to section 2-83.

(b) Special meetings. Special meetings may be proposed by any member of the board or agency by each member of  the board or agency being served written notice  of  the  proposed  meeting  at  least  twenty-four (24) hours prior to the time of  the meeting. Meetings shall not begin before 6:00 p.m. The notice shall state the purpose of the meeting and only business enumerated in the notice shall be transacted at such meeting. A notice of special meeting shall first be delivered to the city manager, who shall arrange for notification of the board or agency members in accordance with requirements stated above.
ADMINISTRATION
Sec.  2-87.  Vote required for board or agency action.

All matters requiring a vote of any board, authority, committee or agency of the city shall be deemed passed only after receiving the affirmative vote of  a majority of  all  of  the  members  thereof.  Matters  receiving  an affirmative  vote  of  the  members  present  (as  distinguished from a majority vote of  the entire membership), shall be continued until the next meeting at which time the matter shall be again considered without further discussion. Any matter failing to receive an affirmative  vote  of  the  entire  membership  of  the  board, authority, committee or agency of the city, shall thereafter be deemed defeated, notwithstanding that a majority of the members present may have acted affirmatively.  Failure  of  any  member of  a board, authority, committee or agency of the city to attend a meeting to consider  voting  on  any  matter  after  continuation  of said matter as aforesaid, shall constitute grounds for removal pursuant to division 2 of this article.
Sec.  2-88.  Notice of violation permitted.

(a)  Whenever  a  license,  permit  or  a  certificate  is required or any act or forebearance is required by any of the provisions of this Code or any other ordinance and it appears to any officer or employee of  the city that  persons  or  corporations  have  failed  to  comply therewith, there may be issued to said person or corporation a notice of violation of the applicable provision of  this Code or such other ordinance. Such notice of violation shall be permitted to be issued only once, in order to permit compliance with the applicable provisions of  this Code or other ordinance within five (5) days. The notice provided by this section is permissive and  failure  to  issue  a  notice  shall  not  constitute  a defense  to  any  action  brought  for  violation  of  this Code or other ordinance. Service of a notice of violation shall in no event be required as a condition precedent to institution of  any action seeking enforcement by way of fine or imprisonment for such violation.

(b)  In the event any person or corporation who has received a notice of violation aforementioned shall fail to obtain from the city the applicable license, permit or certificate or perform the act or desist as required, the proper  officer  of  the  city  shall  cause  to  be  issued  a complaint charging violation of this Code or the applicable municipal ordinance.
Sec.  2-89.  Complaints by city officers of violations.

Where there is alleged to be a violation of this Code, the proper officer of  the city may, in addition to all other  remedies  permitted,  cause  to  be  filed  with  the court having jurisdiction a summons and complaint, charging with particularity the violation of  a specific section of this Code. The complaint shall be under oath and shall charge a person or corporation with an offense under this Code on a particular day at a time and place stated. The complaint shall be in writing and in the name of the city and shall set forth substantially the nature of  the offense. The complaint shall be filed by the  officer  making  same  and  shall  set  forth  the  date when executed.
Sec.  2-90.  Licenses, permits nontransferable.
No license  or  permit  shall  be  transferable,  unless otherwise provided.
Sec.  2-91.  Form, contents of applications generally.

All applications (except for business tax receipts and personnel applications) filed with the city, shall be filed in duplicate, and with such additional copies as shall be required by rules. Every blank space shall be filled in and where not applicable, the words "not applicable" shall be used. Applications shall be signed by the real party in interest or its authorized attorney or agent-infact. All applications and exhibits shall become a part of the records of the city and be filed with the records of the board, agency or officer before whom originally filed. Exhibits required to be attached shall be attached in their final form as numbered exhibits to the application and shall thereafter be referred to by number. No action shall be taken on any application by any officer, board or agency of  the city until  the  above  requirements  have  been  met.  Letters  and  informal  applications shall substantially comply with these rules. Whenever it  is  necessary  for  an  appeal  to  be  taken  to  any board, agency or to the city commission, as required by the  Charter  or  this  Code,  all  supporting  documents shall be attached thereto as exhibits and referred to as an "exhibit" by number.
Sec.  2-92.  Change  of  address  or  personnel  by  applicant.
If any applicant moves or changes location, or if any corporate applicant shall have any change in the office
OPA-LOCKA CODE

of  president,  a  rider  describing  said  change  shall  be filed forthwith with the department of  buildings and licenses, prior to the city granting the relief sought. (Code 1955, § 2-82; Code 1983, § 2-92)
Sec.  2-93.  Certification of application examination and form.
When an officer of the city is required to issue any permit or license, the officer shall cause to be recorded upon the application the following certificate:

Sec.  2-97.  Business  tax  receipts,  permits  or  certificates; due dates and delinquency; penalties.

If September 30 falls on a weekend or holiday, the tax is due and payable on or before the first working day following September 30. Business tax receipts that are not renewed when due and payable are delinquent and subject to a delinquency penalty of ten (10) percent for the month of  October, plus an additional five (5) percent penalty for each subsequent month of  delinquency until paid. However, the total delinquency penalty  may  not  exceed  twenty-five  (25)  percent  of  the business tax for the delinquent establishment.

(b)  Any  person  who  engages  in  or  manages  any business, occupation, or profession without first obtaining a local business tax receipt, if required, is subject to a penalty of twenty-five (25) percent of the license due, in  addition  to  any  other  penalty  provided  by  law  or ordinance.

(c)  Any person who engages in any business, occupation, or profession covered by this section, who does not pay the required business tax within one hundred fifty (150) days after the initial notice of  tax due and who does not obtain the required business tax receipt is subject to civil actions and penalties, including court costs, reasonable attorney fees, additional administrative costs incurred as a result of collection efforts, and a penalty of up to two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00).

(d)  The provisions of this section are applicable to the issuance of any license, permit or certificate. Should it appear that the proper persons, corporations or entities  required  to  obtain  same  have  not  obtained  the applicable license, permit or certificate within the time required by law, the assessment as outlined above shall be instituted and enforced.

DIVISION 2.  REMOVAL OF BOARD OR AGENCY MEMBERS
Sec.  2-109.  Applicability.

Any  member  of  a  board  or  agency  of  the  city, subject to removal for cause, may be removed by the city commission in accordance with the applicable Charter and ordinance provision relating to said board or agency as provided by this division.
Sec.  2-110.  Affidavit of charges required.

Any person desiring the removal of  any board or agency member for cause, shall submit to the city manager  an  affidavit  setting  forth  the  charge  or  charges which the complainant believes, if true, would constitute sufficient cause for removal of the individual as a member of a board or agency by the city commission, and all facts in support of the charges.
Sec.  2-111.  Referral of affidavit to city commission.

The city commission shall receive said affidavit from the city manager at the next regular or special commission meeting occurring not more than three (3) days after the filing of the affidavit with the city manager. It
shall  be  the  duty  of  the  city  manager  to  place  the affidavit on the agenda of the city commission meeting for consideration.
Sec.  2-112.  Action of commission on affidavit.
The city commission, after consideration of the affidavit, may, by any of the following motions:
(a) Move that no further action be taken. In the event  no  motion  is  made  or  seconded,  the matter shall be deemed dismissed.
(b) Determine that the charges, if true, are insufficient to cause the removal of  the board or agency  member,  in  which  event  the  matter shall be deemed dismissed.

(c) Determine that the charges, if  true, are sufficient to cause removal and set public hearing, wherein the truth of the charges shall be determined. Upon the passage of this motion, the board or agency member shall be deemed suspended from office and shall not take part in any matter pending before his board or agency.
Sec.  2-113.  Calling, notice of hearing.

In  the  event  the  commission  determines  that  the charges, if  true,  are  sufficient  to  constitute  cause  for removal, the commission shall forthwith cause the board member or agency member to be notified of the charges and  a  copy  thereof  shall  be  served  upon  him  with notice of  hearing before the commission. All persons having  knowledge  of  the  charges  brought,  shall  be permitted  to  testify  before  the  commission  and  the commission shall be permitted to make such investigations  as  it  deems  necessary  under  the  provisions  of section 2-3.
Sec.  2-114.  Conduct of hearing.

The hearing shall be conducted by the mayor who shall direct the city clerk to place under oath, all persons  who  shall  appear  before  the  commission.  Witnesses may be excluded from the commission chambers prior to testifying. The affidavit shall be read in full by the city attorney. Thereafter, the complainant may make a statement. The complainant shall be subject to crossexamination  by  the  board  or  agency  member  or  his
OPA-LOCKA CODE

counsel. Any member of  the commission or the city attorney  may  question  the  complainant.  Thereafter, the  mayor shall  call  any  witnesses  in  support  of  the charges brought, which witnesses may be examined by the mayor and/or any commissioner and the city attorney. The witnesses shall be subject to cross-examination by the board or agency member. At the conclusion of  the  testimony  of  all  witnesses  in  support  of  the charges, the agency member or board member may or may not testify in his own behalf. In the event the board or agency member testifies in his own behalf, he shall be  subject  to  cross-examination  by  the  complainant and questioning of the commission and city attorney. Both the complainant and the board or agency member may request the mayor to call any additional witnesses they may deem necessary, who shall be examined in the same manner as the witnesses in support of the charges,  subject  to  cross-examination  by  the  mayor, commission and city attorney.
Sec.  2-115.  Conclusion of testimony.

At the conclusion of the testimony, the commission may discuss the matter, adjourn to another fixed time and place for the purpose of  investigation or hearing additional testimony or for additional discussion, or close the public hearing.
Sec.  2-116.  Final determination of commission.
At the conclusion of  the discussion from the commission, the commission may make any of the following motions:
(a) Move that no further action be taken, or in the event  no  motion  is  made  and  seconded,  the matter shall be deemed dismissed.
(b) Determine that those portions of the charges proved are insufficient to cause removal and the matter shall be deemed dismissed.
(c) Determine that the charges have been proven and the board or agency member may be either:
(1) Suspended  from  office  for  a  period  of time; or
(2) Dismissed and removed. (Code 1955, § 2-94; Code 1983, § 2-116)
Sec.  2-117.  Commissioner bringing charges to abstain.

At all times during the aforementioned procedure, no commissioner, who shall have caused the charges to be brought, shall participate at any stage of  the proceedings and shall cause himself  to abstain from participation in any vote in the proceedings.
Sec.  2-118.  Failure to appear at hearing.
Failure of  the board or agency member whose removal is sought to appear at the public hearing shall automatically  constitute  grounds  for  dismissal  from office without further public hearing.
Sec.  2-119.  Requests for testimony of city employees.

The board or agency member may request the city manager to require any employee of the city to appear and give testimony before the city commission in any matter relating to the proceedings, provided a request designates the name of the employee and shall be filed in writing with the city manager twenty-four (24) hours prior to the time of hearing before the city commission. (Code 1955, § 2-94; Code 1983, § 2-119)
Sec.  2-120.  Automatic removal for absences.

In the event any member of any board or agency of the city shall fail to attend three (3) consecutive meetings after receipt of notice thereof, whether special or regular meeting, and said absence shall not have been excused by majority vote of  the board, or excused by the city commission, then the term of said board member shall be deemed completed and the city commission shall appoint a replacement as soon as practicable. Absence as a result  of  illness  requiring  confinement shall be deemed excusable unless said illness shall require confinement for more than eight (8) consecutive regular or special meetings, in which event the term of the member shall be deemed completed.

Sec.  2-192.  First source hiring referral program.
(a) Title. This section shall be referred to as the first source hiring referral program.

(b) Definitions. The  following  words,  terms  and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

(1) Implementing  order or IO means  the  implementing order developed by the mayor or mayor's designee and approved by city commissioners (the "commissioner") to give effect to the provisions of this section.
(2) City contract means an agreement for the purchase of goods and services specifically identified in the implementing order.
(3) Contractor means any person or entity which enters into a contract with the city.
(4) First source register means the register of unemployed persons maintained by the referral agency in accordance with the provisions of this section.
(5) Referral agency means the South Florida Workforce Investment Board (SFWIB).
(6) Referral period means the three (3) to five (5) day period following notification to the referral agency of employment availability.

(c) First source register created. The referral agency shall compile and maintain a first source register, which shall  be  a  listing  of  unemployed  persons,  including graduates of programs funded by the Workforce Investment Act to be made available to contractors as a first source for their employment needs. The referral agency shall not discriminate on the basis of  race, ethnicity, sex, residence, or other protected category or class, in the  compilation  or  maintenance  of  the  first  source register, or in its referral activities provided for in this section. The referral agency shall, to the extent allowed by law, maintain a data base which identifies the race, ethnicity, sex, and residence of the persons within the first source register sufficient to permit adequate analysis of the available work force.
(d) Referral procedure.
(1) The referral agency shall be the first source for employees  to  fill  jobs  created  to  satisfy  the requirements of city contracts. The following
OPA-LOCKA CODE

requirements shall be included in all city contracts, except those covered under the community  workforce  program  (CWP),  and  except those covered under programs intended to encourage and assist in the employment of  the blind and other severely handicapped persons such as described in F.S. §§ 413.032-413.037:

a. The  contractor,  prior  to  hiring  to  fill each vacancy arising under a city contract, shall first notify the referral agency of the vacancy and list the vacancy with the referral agency. The listing shall contain  a  detailed  description  of  the  job responsibilities and qualifications and be posted  during  the  referral  period.  The referral  agency  shall  provide  a  list  of qualified candidates, if  such candidates are available, to contractor within twentyfour  (24)  hours  of  receiving  notice  of vacancy. Thereafter, contractor shall (a) review the resumes and qualifications of the  candidates;  and  (b)  make  a  good faith effort as determined by the city, to fill a minimum of fifty (50) percent of its employment needs under the city contract from the first source register. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if  after the referral period a suitable employee is not found from the referral agency, the contractor is free to fill its vacancies from other sources.

b. A good faith effort to employ candidates from the referral agency shall constitute, at a minimum, evaluating the qualification of such candidates, and conducting interviews with those candidates who satisfy  the  minimum competency requirements. The contractor is not required to hire  any  individual  candidate  referred. However, contractors shall not commit to  fill  vacancies  in  any  other  manner until after the end of the referral period, unless  the  referral  agency  notifies  the contractor in writing prior to the end of the referral period that qualified candidates are not available in sufficient numbers to fill the vacancies. Upon such notification, the contractor may immediately  fill  vacancies  using  other sources.
Supp. No. 1

c. In determining whether a contractor has made  good  faith  efforts,  the  city  may consider, among other criteria to be set forth in the implementing order: (a) the number,  skills  and  composition  of  the contractor's labor force ultimately hired; (b) whether minimum requirements were established  for  available  positions  beyond  reasonable  requirements  to  complete the job; (c) the number of referred candidates interviewed for the position; and (d) the contractor's use of  the first source register to satisfy its labor needs in  contracts  other  than  city  contracts. The city's determination as to whether a contractor has made such good faith efforts is final and binding.
d. All  competitive  solicitations  for  contracts, except those covered under CWP, shall set forth the requirements of  this section.
(e) Monitoring and compliance.

(1) City contracts shall require the contractor to submit quarterly reports to the referral agency indicating the name and number of employees hired by the contractor in the previous quarter, including the source from which such employees were found, and payroll records and tallies of employee work hours. If none of the candidates referred to a contractor by the referral agency were hired, the contractor shall report the reasons why all referred candidates were  rejected  in  its  quarterly  reports.  Each quarterly report shall be submitted to referral agency within two (2) weeks of the end of the quarter.

(2) For each contract, the contractor shall retain records sufficient to determine compliance with this  section.  Such  records  shall  include:  (1) notifications to the referral agency; (2) referrals from the referral agency; (3) job applications  received  from  sources  other  than  the referral agency; and (4) the number of candidates hired based on referrals from the referral agency.  To  the  extent  allowed  by  law,  such records  shall  be  made  available  to  referral agency upon request.

DIVISION 2.  SEVERANCE PAY; EXTRA COMPENSATION
Sec.  2-222.  Prohibiting severance pay and extra compensation beyond state statutory limits.

(a)  No severance pay shall be provided to the city manager, city attorney, city clerk (collectively, "charter officers") or any other employee where the individual is terminated for cause. "Cause" shall include, but is not
OPA-LOCKA CODE
limited to: misconduct, malfeasance, gross negligence, breach of contract, violation of law, or any other justifiable basis as defined in the officer's employment agreement, city policy or state law.

(b)  Pursuant  to  F .S.  §  215.425,  the  city  shall  not provide any bonus, extra compensation, or additional payment to any charter officer of the city after services have been rendered or after a contract has been executed, unless otherwise authorized by Florida law or by a majority vote of the city commission.

(c)  Any contract or employment agreement, or renewal or renegotiation of  an existing contract or employment agreement, that contains a provision for severance pay with an officer, agent, employee, or contractor must include the following provisions in the contract: (1) a requirement that severance pay provided may not exceed an amount greater than twenty (20) weeks of compensation; (2) a prohibition of provision of severance pay when the officer, agent, employee, or contractor has been fired for misconduct, as defined in F.S. § 443.036(29), by the unit of government.

(d)  Severance pay for a charter officer shall be permitted  only  in  the  following  cases,  and  only  upon  a majority  vote  of  the  city  commission:  (1)  voluntary resignation where severance is a part of  the contract terms;  and  (2)  termination  without  cause  where  the severance  pay  does  not  exceed  the  limits  established under applicable state law.

(e)  As a condition of  receiving any severance pay, the charter officer must execute a written separation agreement  that  includes  a  comprehensive  release  of liability in favor of the city, its officials, employees, and agents. The release must be in a form approved by the city attorney and shall fully release the city from any and all claims arising from the officer's employment or separation from the city. The officer shall have thirtyone (31) calendar days from the date of separation or notice of termination to execute and deliver the signed separation agreement to the city clerk. An agreement is not  executed  and  returned  within  the  thirty-one-day period, the officer shall be deemed to have waived all rights  to  severance  pay,  and  the  city  shall  have  no further obligation to provide such payment. The city shall  issue  any  approved  severance  payment  within thirty (30) calendar days of receiving the fully executed agreement.

DIVISION 8.  DRUG FREE WORKPLACE
Sec.  2-297.5.  Intent.

It is the intent of the city to maintain a healthy and productive  workforce  with  safe  working  conditions, free from the effects of drugs. Drug use creates a variety of  workplace problems, including increased injury on the job, increased absenteeism, increased financial burden on health and benefits programs, increased workplace theft, decreased employee morale, decreased productivity and a decline in the quality of products and services. By promoting a drug free workplace, through fair and reasonable drug testing methods for the protection of the city and its employees, the city intends to discourage drug abuse. Employees who choose to engage in drug abuse face the risk of unemployment and the forfeiture of  benefits, including worker's compensation benefits.
Sec.  2-297.6.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in  this  division,  shall  have  the  meanings  ascribed  to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

Chain of custody refers to the methodology of tracking specified materials or substances for the purpose of maintaining  control  and  accountability  from  initial collection to final disposition for all such materials or substances and providing accountability at each stage in handling, testing, storing specimens and reporting of test results.

Drug means alcohol, including distilled spirits, wine, malt  beverages,  and  intoxicating  liquors;  amphetamines,  cannabinoids,  cocaine,  phencyclidine  (PCP), hallucinogens,  methaqualone,  opiates,  barbiturates, benzodiazepines, synthetic narcotics, designer drugs or a  metabolite  of  any  of  the  substances  listed  in  this definition.
Drug test means any chemical, biological or physical instrumental analysis administered for the purpose of determining the presence or absence of  a drug or its metabolites.
ADMINISTRATION

Employees shall  include  all  personnel  working for the city, including all classified, unclassified and police personnel, all appointed officers, and members of  all boards, commissions and committees. The city commission  members may choose to comply voluntarily with the provisions of this division.
Sec.  2-297.7.  Testing.

(a)  Job  applicants  of  the  city  shall  undergo  preemployment drug testing  as  a  condition  of  employment, to include testing for any drug described in section 2-297.6. Refusal to submit to testing or a positive confirmed drug test may be used as a basis for refusing to hire.
(b)  Employees shall undergo drug testing according to the standards set forth in the applicable collective bargaining agreement, if any, for any drug described in section 2-297.6.

(c)  If  an employee voluntarily enters an employee assistance program for drug-related problems or a drug rehabilitation  program,  the  city  may  require  a  follow-up drug test, with no advance notice to the employee.

(d)  The cost of  initial and confirmation drug testing required by the city shall be paid by the city. Any additional drug tests not required by the city shall be paid by the job applicant or employee.
(e)  Drug tests shall be conducted by licensed laboratories, using chain of custody procedures. (Code 1983, § 2-297.7; Ord. No. 10-06, § 2, 3-10-2010)
Sec.  2-297.8.  Establishment of rules.

The city is permitted to establish reasonable work rules related to the possession, use, sale, trafficking or solicitation of drugs or other drug-related offenses by employees and to take action based upon a violation of the rules.
Sec.  2-297.9.  Confidentiality.
Except as provided in F.S. ch. 112, all information received as a result of a drug testing program is confidential  and  exempt  from  the  provisions  of F.S. § 119.07(1).

ARTICLE V.  CHARTER REVISIONS AND AMENDMENTS
Sec.  2-298.  Methods for drafting.

Pursuant to the requirements of section 6.03 of the Home Rule Charter of Miami-Dade County, Florida, the procedure for the drafting, or having drafted, of a proposed charter, amendment, revocation or abolition of the government of the city, is hereby determined to be by the method of:

(a) Accepting the question for submission to referendum, without amendment, revocation or abolition, contained in a petition certified to contain the signatures of  ten (10) percent of the qualified electors of the city.

(b) Having prepared by the city attorney and approved by the city commission (either with or without the prior preparation and approval of a charter board or committee), a resolution or resolutions calling referendums providing for the adoption, amendment or revocation of the Charter of the city or to abolish its existence.
Sec.  2-299.  Creation of a Charter review board.
The  city  commission  hereby  creates  an  advisory board to the commission to be known as the Charter review board.
Sec.  2-300.  Membership, term, duties and responsibilities.

(a)  Membership.  The  Charter  review  board  shall consist of five (5) resident electors (each appointed by one member of the city commission) and two (2) advisory  (non-voting)  members  appointed  by  a  majority vote of  the city commission. Each board member so appointed shall be a qualified elector of the city with an outstanding reputation for civic pride, interest, integrity, responsibility and business or professional ability. advisory board members may reside outside of the city.

(b)  Term. Upon city commission appointment, the term of each individual member to the Charter review board  shall  commence.  Each  member  so  appointed shall be appointed for a term of (1) one year from the date of  appointment. The Charter review board shall
provide  its  report  and  recommendations  to  the  city clerk. Any recommended Charter changes shall be prepared for consideration by the city commission.

(c)  Duties. The Charter review board may provide recommendations  to  the  city  commission  regarding amendments and revisions to the Charter, which may be advisable for placement on the election ballot.
(d)  Responsibilities.

(1) The Charter review board shall have an organization  meeting.  The  Charter  review  board shall elect a chair and a vice-chair from among its membership. The meetings shall be held on the call of the chair or a majority of its members at a noticed meeting. All meetings shall be open to the public and held in the city commission chambers. A majority of  members shall constitute a quorum to do business.

(2) Notice of all meetings shall be posted at least 48  hours  in  advance  in  city  hall  and  on  the city's website. The city shall provide a written record of each meeting through summary minutes.
(3) The meetings shall be conducted governed by Robert's Rules of Order.

(4) The Charter review board shall make recommendations to the city commission. No amendments or revisions to the city Charter shall be submitted to the city commission for consideration unless favorably voted upon by an affirmative vote of a majority of the board members.

(5) Any  elector  of  the  city  who  in  good  faith believes that an amendment should be made to the Charter of the city shall indicate his or her recommendation in writing and shall file the same with the clerk of  the city who shall forward a copy of same to each of the members of the charter board and at the next regularly scheduled public meeting of the board, said elector shall be heard and may give evidence concerning his recommendations. The board shall also hear the recommendations of the city commission, the city attorney, the city manager and the city clerk, when presented.

(6) The board shall make all recommendations to the city commission as to revisions to the Charter within one hundred twenty (120) days from passage of said recommendations.

(7) The members shall serve without compensation but sufficient funds shall be provided by the city commission in the annual budget for reasonable  and  necessary  expenses  to  be  incurred  by  the  board  in  performance  of  its duties.  The  city  manager  shall  provide  such administrative  and  clerical  staff  as  may  be necessary  in  the  proper  performance  of  its duties.

Sec.  2-314.  Legislative intent.

(a)  The  city  commission  recognizes  that  fair  and open competition is a basic tenet of  public procurement; that such competition reduces the appearance and opportunity for favoritism and inspires public confidence that contracts are awarded equitably and economically; and that documentation of  the acts taken and  effective  monitoring  mechanisms  are  important means of  curbing any improprieties and establishing public confidence in the process of which contractual services are procured. It is essential to the effective and ethical procurement of contractual services that there be a system of uniform procedures to be utilized by city agencies in managing and procuring contractual services; that detailed justification of department or division decisions in the procurement of  contractual services  be  maintained;  and  that  adherence  by  the department or division and the consultant to specific ethical considerations be required.

(b)  To ensure efficient and economical purchasing practices, the city manager shall prepare and submit proposed  rules  and  regulations  as  necessary  for  city purchases to the city commission for their consideration. Such rules shall have the force and effect of law

Sec.  2-315.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in  this  division,  shall  have  the  meanings  ascribed  to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Agency means any of  the various city officers, departments,  divisions,  bureaus,  and  any  other  unit  of organization, however designated, of  the city government.
