Terms  of office  shall  correspond  to  the  term  of  office  of  the appointing city commissioner. The advisory board shall select and designate from its membership a chairman and vice-chairman. The board shall be governed by the rules of procedures applicable to all boards within the city.

(b) Meetings; clerical help. The advisory board shall meet once each month at a time to be selected by a majority  of  its  membership.  The  city  manager  shall supply necessary clerical help in order to provide for the taking of  minutes and reporting conclusions and recommendations to the city commission on a monthly basis.

(c) Duties. The advisory board shall advise the city commission in all matters involving the administration of the city government, commission policies, projects, activities  and  events  wherein  youth,  teen  and  young adult participation is requested or desired. In addition, the board shall make recommendations on increasing youth, teen and young adult participation in local governments, seek ways to improve communication with students  and  young  adults  within  the  City,  organize and  perform  services  projects  that  benefit  the  City, recommend the creation of programs for youth, teens and young adults and assume and carry out such duties as may from time to time be directed by the city commission.
(d) Filling  vacancies. Unexpired  terms  created  by resignation, death or removal, shall be filled by the city commissioner or his successor originally making the appointment vacated.
Sec.  16-2.  Recreational programs limited to residents; nonresident use of city facilities.
Only  residents  of  the  city  may  participate  in  any city-organized recreation program. Any outside orga-
nization wishing to use the city parks or facilities must meet the guidelines and have the approval of  the city manager.
Secs.  16-3-16-19.  Reserved.
ARTICLE II.  USE AND CONDUCT REGULATIONS
DIVISION 1.  GENERALLY
Sec.  16-20.  Policy declared.

It is the general purpose and intent of this article to establish uniform procedures for the administration of parks and recreational facilities in the city, to establish a system of regulations and rules governing the activities within the parks and recreational facilities; to declare certain activities as violations of  rules and regulations; to provide for criminal penalties for violation of the rules and regulations; to allow expulsion from a park or recreational facility for violation of a rule; and to  provide  a  procedure  for  establishing  permits  for activities within designated areas and to set methods for the administration of parks and recreational facilities.
Sec.  16-21.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcoholic beverages means any beer, wine, fortified wine, liquor or other alcoholic beverage defined in F.S. ch. 561.
Closing hours means that time period which a park or recreational facility is closed to the general public.
Department means  the  department  of  parks  and recreation of the city.
Designated area means that geographical area which has been designated by the department for a specific activity or activities within a park or recreation area.
CODE CITE
Director means  the  manager  or  the  person  appointed by him to coordinate all park and recreation programs and facilities.
Governmental  unit means  any  governmental  body which exercises police jurisdiction over a park or recreational facility.
Gun means any instrument capable of firing a projectile  or  bullet  at  a  high  velocity,  including, but not limited to, any air gun, sling or slingshot.
Motor  vehicle means  a  vehicle  which  is  self-propelled.
Park means a park, reservation, playground, beach, recreation center or other area owned, leased or used by  the  department  and  devoted  to  active  or  passive recreation.
Permit means  a  written  document  issued  by  the department granting permission for a specific activity.
Recreational facility means a facility for recreational purposes  on  property  owned,  leased  or  used  by  the department.
Regulation means a regulation approved by the commission  which  governs  the  use  of  parks  and  recreational facilities and the violation of which subjects the offender to criminal penalties.

Rule means  a  rule  approved  by  the  commission which governs the use of parks or recreational facilities and  the  violation  of  which  subjects  the  offender  to rejection or expulsion from park or recreational facilities.
Vehicle means any wheeled conveyance, whether motor powered, animal drawn or self-propelled. The term "vehicle" shall include any trailer in tow or any size, kind or description.
Sec.  16-22.  Reserved.
Sec.  16-23.  Rules authorized; ejection of violators.

(a)  The commission, by resolution, shall adopt rules governing the use of  parks and recreational facilities owned, leased or operated by the city, which may include, but are not limited to, the use of  supplies and equipment, the charge and payment of fees, the hours of operation, the use and parking of vehicles, the con-
duct and overall safety of persons within parks and the general use of parks and recreational facilities for each such park or recreational facility as may be necessary.
(b)  Any person violating a rule may be expelled or ejected from any park or recreational facility. (Code 1955, § 16A-23; Code 1983, § 16-23)
Sec.  16-24.  Temporary closing and exclusion of public.

In an emergency, when the department shall determine that the public interest, health, morals and safety require such action, any park or recreational area or any part thereof may be closed and all persons may be excluded from such area.
Sec.  16-25.  City's right to enter.

The  department  and  its  employees  shall  have  the right at all times to enter the premises of any building, structure or enclosure of  any park or recreational facility, including such grounds, buildings, structures or enclosures as may be leased or set aside for private or exclusive use of any individual or group.
Sec.  16-26.  Designation of areas for specific use.

The director shall have the power to designate areas and  facilities  in  parks  and  recreational  facilities  for specific activities, and to prohibit other activities within the designated area. The director shall be the official custodian of a list of all areas which have been designated for  specific  activities.  Such  list  shall  contain  a description of  the property which is designated for a specific activity and the nature of  the activities which are permitted. The director is authorized to post designated  areas  when,  in  his  discretion,  such  posting  is appropriate.
Sec.  16-27.  Activities confined to designated areas.

No person shall play or participate in any game or organized activity, including, but not limited to, football, baseball, basketball or any such game, in any park or recreational facility, except in areas designated for such use.
PARKS AND RECREATION
Sec.  16-28.  Permit required for group use.

Any lodge, society, social organization, social club, group or other organization of  ten (10) or more persons, desiring to use any park or recreational facility for a picnic or other recreational purpose shall obtain a permit from the department not less than seven (7) days prior to such use. Such permit shall be signed by the director or his duly authorized representative.
Sec.  16-29.  Conditions to permit issuance.
The department may issue a permit for group use when it has been established:
(a) That the proposed activity will occur within an area in which it is proper for the activity to occur.
(b) That the proposed activity or use will not unreasonably interfere or detract from the general  public  enjoyment  of  the  park  or  recreational area.

(c) That there are adequate facilities and personnel in the proposed areas so that the proposed activity will not impair the health, safety and welfare of the persons who will engage in the proposed activities, nor will the proposed activity impair the health, safety, welfare or recreation of the general public.
(d) That the desired facility has not been reserved for other use at the time requested.

(e) In the event any proposed activity may constitute a hazard to any person or property, the department, as a condition to the issuance of a permit, may require public liability insurance in an amount the department deems appropriate to protect such person or property.
Sec.  16-30.  Notice of permit denial.

In  the  event  any  applicant  is  refused  a  group  use permit, the department shall notify the applicant within ten (10) days of the reason for refusing such permit. (Code 1955, § 16A-26; Code 1983, § 16-30)
Sec.  16-31.  Appeal of permit denial.
The applicant may appeal the refusal of a group use permit to the  commission within ten (10) days after
notification of such refusal is sent, by filing a petition with the city clerk, stating why the applicant should receive a permit.
Sec.  16-32.  Permit revocation.
The department or its duly authorized representative  shall  have  the  authority  to  revoke  a  group  use permit upon finding a violation of any rule or regulation.
Sec.  16-33.  Reserved.
Secs.  16-34-16-42.  Reserved.
DIVISION 2.  SPECIFIC REGULATIONS
Sec.  16-43.  Interfering with city personnel.
No person shall hinder or oppose any officer, agent or employee of the department in the discharge of his duties or with the enforcement of the park regulations and rules.
Sec.  16-44.  Entering, remaining during closing hours.

No person shall enter or remain in a park or recreational area without a permit during closing hours if the closing hours are posted at the entrance of the park or recreational facility. No person shall enter or remain in  a  park  or  recreational  facility  after  such  person receives notice of the closing hours from a department employee.
Sec.  16-45.  Duty to leave on request.

No person who has violated a rule shall remain in a park  or  recreational  facility  after  a  department  employee, police officer, sheriff's deputy, or employee of a governmental  unit  requests  such  person  to  leave  or vacate a park or recreational facility.
Sec.  16-46.  Damaging property.
No person in any park or recreational facility shall willfully mark, deface, disfigure, tamper with, displace or remove any building, bridges, tables, benches, fire-
CODE CITE

places, railings, paving or paving material, water lines, or  other  public  utilities  or  parts  or  appurtenances thereof, signs, notices, or placards whether temporary or permanent, monuments, stakes, posts or other structures or equipment or any part of any of the aforesaid facilities, park property or appurtenances whatsoever, either  real  or  personal  in  any  park  or  recreational facility.
(Code 1955, § 16A-24; Code 1983, § 16-46) State law reference- Criminal mischief, F.S. § 806.13.
Sec.  16-47.  Damaging vegetation.

No person  in  any  park  or  recreational  area  shall remove, cut, carve or transplant, any tree, shrubbery, lawn, plant or injure the bark or pick the flowers. No person shall attach any rope, wire or other contrivance to any tree or plant in any park or recreational facility. (Code 1955, § 16A-24; Code 1983, § 16-47)
State law reference- Criminal mischief, F.S. § 806.13.
Sec.  16-48.  Removing natural resources.

No person in any park or recreational facility shall remove any beach sand, whether submerged or not, any soil, rock, stones, plants, wood or other materials, or make any excavation by tool, equipment, blasting or other means or agency.
Sec.  16-49.  Polluting waters.

No person in any park or recreational facility shall throw or place or cause to be thrown or placed, any dirt, filth or foreign matter into the waters of any lake, pond, pool, river, inlet, tank or reservoir in any park or recreational facility.
Sec.  16-50.  Disposal of rubbish.

No person in any park or recreational facility shall throw, place, cast, deposit, dump or cause to be thrown, any ashes, refuse, offal, vegetables, garbage, dross, cinders, shells, straw, shavings, paper, scraps, dirt or like matter, filth or rubbish of any kind in any park, square, avenue, grounds, or recreational area, except to place the same in cans or receptacles provided for such matter.
Sec.  16-51.  Hunting, molesting wildlife.

No person  in  any  park  or  recreational  area  shall hunt,  catch,  harm,  kill,  trap,  chase,  tease,  shoot  or throw  missiles  at  any  animal,  reptile  or  bird  except poisonous  snakes.  No  person  in  any  park  or  recreational areas shall remove or have in his possession the young of any wild animal or eggs or nest or young of any reptile or bird.
Sec.  16-52.  Alcoholic beverages.
No alcoholic beverages shall be sold, stored or consumed within any park or city recreation area, except by approval of city manager for sales or consumption at special events.
Sec.  16-53.  Reserved.
Sec.  16-54.  Fires.
No person  in  any  park  or  recreational  area  shall ignite, set or maintain any fire for cooking or any other purpose unless such fire is within a designated area for such purpose.
Sec.  16-55.  Fireworks.

No person  in  any  park  or  recreational  area  shall carry,  fire  or  discharge  any  rocket,  torpedo  or  other fireworks of any description without a permit from the department to discharge in an area designated for such purpose.
Sec.  16-56.  Reserved.
Sec.  16-57.  Conducting,  participating  in  unpermitted meeting.

No person shall conduct or participate in any public meeting,  assembly,  entertainment,  tournament,  religious gathering, demonstration, parade, procession or meeting on any subject, religious, social, political or otherwise, in  any  park  or  recreational  area,  unless  a permit from the department has been issued for such meeting,  assembly,  entertainment,  tournament,  reli-

gious gathering, demonstration, parade or procession. Such  a  permit  shall  be  issued  upon  a  showing  that public safety will not be endangered.

No person shall use any loudspeaker or other amwithout a permit from the department.
plifying equipment nor shall any person play upon any musical  instrument  in  any  park  or  recreational  area (Code 1955, § 16A-24; Code 1983, § 16-58)
Sec.  16-59.  Sales.

No  person  shall  sell,  keep,  or  offer  for  sale  any tangible or intangible object, merchandise or thing for any consideration within any park or recreational area without a permit from the department.
Sec.  16-60.  Signs or posters.

No person  shall  post  or  affix  to  any  tree,  shrub, plant, fence, building, structure, monument, wall, table, apparatus, bridge, post, bench, corral, gate or any other physical  object,  any  sign,  poster  or  other  printed  or written matter in any park or recreational facility. (Code 1955, § 16A-24; Code 1983, § 16-60)
Sec.  16-61.  Sleeping, camping, overnight parking.

No person shall sleep, camp, lodge or park a vehicle overnight  in  any  park  or  recreational  area  except  in such areas as are designated for such purposes or without a permit from the department.
Sec.  16-62.  Traffic.
(a)  Reserved.
(b)  Reserved.
(c)  Park employees may direct traffic in public works only in the absence of  a police officer and when required for protection of the public.

(d)  No person shall operate, drive or park any motor vehicle or other vehicle upon any road, driveway, path,  parking  area  or  other  area  unless  such  road, driveway,  path,  parking  area  or  other  area  has  been designated  by  the  department  for  such  purpose.  No
person shall cause any vehicle for hire to stand upon any part of a park or recreational area for the purpose of soliciting passengers.
(e)  No person shall drive a vehicle at a rate of speed exceeding five (5) miles per hour in any city park, unless the department has designated, by posted sign, a greater speed limit.

(f)  No person shall park any vehicle in other than the area which is designated for parking. No person shall  leave  any  vehicle  standing  or  parked  at  night without lights clearly visible at least two hundred (200) feet upon said vehicle except in legally established parking areas or designated campsite areas.
(g)  No person shall enter or exit from any park or recreational facility in any vehicle except on entrances and exits established for such purpose by the department.
Sec.  16-63.  Water activities.
No person shall swim, ski, dive, surf, scuba dive, fish or use boats in any area in any park or recreational area unless such area is specifically designated for such purpose.
Sec.  16-64.  Utilities.
No person shall locate any utility upon any park or recreational  facility  without  receiving  a  permit  from the department.
Sec.  16-65.  Aircraft and parachuting.
No person shall ascend or land any aircraft, glider or  parachute  over  or  into  any  park  or  recreational facility without a permit from the department. (Code 1955, § 16A-24; Code 1983, § 16-65)
Sec.  16-66.  Smoking prohibited in outdoor areas in the city parks.

(a)  It  shall  be  unlawful  for  any  person  to  smoke cigarettes, cigars, pipes or any other smoking apparatus on playing fields and playgrounds, bleacher areas, dugouts, around team seating areas, concession areas, spectator areas, restrooms, or any other areas not spe-

cifically designated as a permitted smoking area within any park owned and operated by the city. All designated smoking areas will be specifically demarcated by signs stating that "Smoking is permitted in this area."

(b)  Upon an individual's first violation of this section, a city official or law enforcement officer may issue a warning to any person in violation of the provisions of this section. Any refusal by an individual to comply with this section upon issuance of a warning may result in a notice to appear being issued by a law enforcement officer for the violation and/or removal from the park. Upon the first conviction of this violation, a court of competent jurisdiction may impose a fine of  twentyfive dollars ($25.00).

ARTICLE I.  IN GENERAL
Sec.  17-1.  Procedure  for  submission  of  planning  and zoning board action to city commission.

All actions, resolutions, findings of fact and recommendations of the planning and zoning board requiring action by the city commission, including appeals, rezonings,  variances,  consideration  of  capital  programs  and  recommendations,  approval  of  land  purchase and all other matters required by the charter and ordinances of the city to be considered by the planning and zoning board shall be submitted to the city commission in accordance with the following procedure:
(a) All  applicants  filing  notice  of  appeal  to  the city commission shall pay to the city clerk the full cost of advertising the public notice.

(b) All applicants for change or modification of zoning prior to consideration of  said matter by the city commission shall pay to the city clerk  the  full  cost  of  advertising  the  public hearing.

(c) The city commission shall consider all appeals and  applications  for  affirmative  relief or changes  or  modifications  in  zoning  as  may have been acted upon or recommended by the planning and zoning board as follows:
(1) All  matters  shall  be  considered  at  any regular or special city commission meeting not more than thirty (30) days, nor less than seven (7) days thereafter.

(2) Where an ordinance is required, the city commission  may  consider  a  necessary ordinance at first reading, however, second reading and final passage shall not be considered until compliance with the requirements of public notice set forth in section 2-132 or F.S. § 166.041, whichever is appropriate. All notices shall be sent by certified mail.

(d) All other matters requiring action by the city commission shall be placed on the agenda of the city commission for the next regular meeting or within twenty (20) days after the planning and zoning board action.
(e) No city or other governmental officer or agency or  committee  on  behalf  of  a  governmental unit shall be required to pay an appeal fee or
fee for public notice in any proceeding originating before the planning and zoning board or prior to consideration by the city commission.
(f) In the event any public hearing is continued by the  city  commission,  notice  thereof  shall  be given in accordance with the provisions of this Code.

Sec.  17-41.  Petition application for vacating streets and alleys-Generally.

All applications for vacating of public right-of-way (public street, road, alleyway, place or highway dedicated  or  acquired  for  travel  or  any  part  or  portion thereof) shall be submitted to the department of planning and zoning. Standard application forms shall be made  available  in  the  department  of  planning  and zoning office. Every petition addressed to the city concerning  any  way  place,  highway,  street,  alley  or  any land acquired for travel or any part or portion thereof to be vacated, closed, discontinued or abandoned, and requesting the city to release any right of the city and the public in and to any land delineated, dedicated or shown on any recorded map or plat as a street, road, alleyway, place or highway within the corporate limits of the city shall be presented to the city commission in the form and following the procedures set forth in this article. The petitioner shall use the petition form available from the department of zoning office.
Sec.  17-42.  Petition application for vacating streets and alleys-Form; address.

Vacating petition applications filed pursuant to this article shall be typewritten and shall be sworn to by the petitioner/applicant  and  shall  include  the  post  office address of the petitioner/applicant.
Sec.  17-43.  Petition application for vacating streets and alleys-Contents.

If the vacating,  closing,  discontinuing  and  abandoning  of  a part or portion of an alleyway desired by the petitioner applicant to be vacated, closed, discontinued and abandoned would result in the creation of a dead-end alleyway, then the petitioner applicant is required to petition apply to vacate, close, discontinue and abandon the entire alleyway or such part or portion thereof  as will preclude the creation of a dead-end alleyway, unless the petitioner applicant provides an adequate turnaround or cul-de-sac.

DIVISION 3.  UNITY OF TITLE
Sec.  17-49.  Definition of unity of title.

The term "unity of title" means a written agreement executed by and between a property owner and the city, whereby the property owner for a specified consideration by the city agrees that the lots and/or parcels of land  constituting  the  building  site  shall  not  be  conveyed,  mortgaged  and/or  leased  separate  and  apart from each other and that they shall be held together as one (1) tract. The form shall be consistent with exhibit A attached to the ordinance from which this division is derived.  Such  unity  of  title  shall  be  recorded  in  the
county public records and shall run with the land and shall be binding upon the property owners, their successors and assigns.
Sec.  17-50.  When required.

As a prerequisite to the issuance of a building permit, the owner in fee simple title shall submit a unity of title in recordable form to the department of planning and zoning providing that all of  the property encompassing the building site upon which the building and appurtenances are to be located shall be held together as one (1) tract of  land and providing that no part or parcel  shall  be  conveyed  or  mortgaged  separate  and apart from the building site, as set forth under the site plan and the building permit in the following cases:

(1) Whenever  the  required  off-street  parking  is located  on  contiguous  lots  or  parcels  or  is located  off-site,  as  provided  for  under  land development  regulations,  article  VI,  relating to off-site parking.

(2) Whenever the building site consists of  more than one (1) lot or parcel and the main building  is  located  on  one  (1)  lot  or  parcel  and accessory use buildings or structures  are  located on the remaining lot or parcel comprising the building site.

(3) Whenever the building site consists of  more than one (1) lot or parcel and the main building is located on one (1) or more of the lots or parcels and the remaining lots or parcels encompassing the building site are required to meet the minimum zoning requirements.

(4) Whenever a building is to be constructed or erected upon a lot or parcel which is larger in frontage, depth and/or area than the minimum required by the zoning ordinance and which lot or parcel would be susceptible to further re-subdivision in accordance with the zoning ordinance and subdivision provisions of  this Code.
(5) Whenever the city provides that a unity of title shall be executed as a condition for the granting of a variance or permit.
(6) Whenever  a  unity  of  title  is  specifically  required by an ordinance or resolution passed and adopted by the city commission.
OPA-LOCKA CODE
(7) Whenever a site plan and/or building site consists of more than one (1) platted lot. (Code 1983, § 17-50; Ord. No. 20-02, § 2, 1-8-2020)
Sec.  17-51.  Specific requirements.

(a)  The owner shall provide a certificate of ownership by way of  an opinion of  title from an attorney licensed to practice law in the state. Said opinion of title, which shall be from the point of beginning, shall be based upon an abstract brought up within ten (10) days  of  the  requirement  that  such  unity  of  title  be recorded.

(b)  The opinion of title shall include the names and addresses of  all mortgagees and lien holders, the description of the mortgages and/or liens and the status of all real estate taxes due and payable.
(c)  The unity of title shall be executed with the same formality and manner as a warranty deed under the
laws of the state. (Code 1983, § 17-51; Ord. No. 20-02, § 2, 1-8-2020)
Sec.  17-52.  Approval, release and recording.
(a)  The unity of title shall be subject to approval by the director of the department of planning and zoning and the city attorney as to form and content.

(b)  Any unity of title required by this section shall not be released except as specified in the legal instrument used to record said unity of title; any unity of title agreement which does not contain a release clause or procedures for release, may be released by the director of  the department of  planning and zoning in a form acceptable to the city attorney, upon a determination by  the  director  of  the  department  of  planning  and zoning that the unity of  title agreement is no longer necessary; in the absence of such a determination, the unity of title shall be released only by resolution passed and  adopted  by  the  city  commission.  Releases  approved pursuant to this section shall be recorded in the county public records at the property owner's expense. (Code 1983, § 17-52; Ord. No. 20-02, § 2, 1-8-2020)

Sec.  18-1.  Department created.
There is hereby created a department of the city to be known as the police department, vested with all of the authority and duties normally vested in municipal police departments or divisions.
Sec.  18-2.  Appointment of chief of police; general duties; absence.

(a)  The head of the city police department shall be known as the chief of police. He shall be appointed by and serve at the will of the city manager. He shall have the immediate direction and control of the city police department, herein created, subject only to the limitations and restrictions set forth in the Charter of the city. He shall devote his entire time to the discharge of his official  duties  and  shall  not  be  absent  from  the  city except in the performance of his official duties, unless granted a written leave of absence by the city manager. He shall be on call at all hours, day and night, and in case  of  his  disability  by  reason  of  sickness,  absence from  the  city  or  other  cause,  the  city  manager  may designate  any  competent  person  to  act  as  chief  of police during such disability, or absence.
(b)  The city manager shall serve as the public safety director ex officio and shall directly supervise the chief of police regarding the enforcement of law and order in the city.

(c)  The city manager is hereby authorized and directed to enter into interlocal mutual aid agreements with each participating law enforcement agency in the county  and  state  at  the  earliest  possible  moment  in order to be prepared to meet the needs of the citizens of the city in the prevention of crime.
Sec.  18-3.  Commissioning of officers.

Each member of  the city police department shall have issued to him a warrant of appointment, signed by the  city  manager  and  attested  by  a  notary  public  in which the date of his appointment shall be stated, and such shall be his commission.

The chief  of  police  and  each  member  of  the  city police department shall, before entering upon his duties, subscribe to an oath as prescribed by F.S. § 876.05. (Code 1955, § 18-6; Code 1983, § 18-4; Ord. No. 90-2, § 1, 1-10-1990)

ARTICLE II.  ALARM SYSTEMS
Sec.  18-33.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alarm company means a person subject to the licensing requirements, and/or a company engaged in selling, leasing, installing, servicing or monitoring alarm systems.
Alarm  permit means  a  permit  issued  by  the  city police department allowing the operation of an alarm system within the city.
Alarm signal means a detectable signal, audible or visual,  generated  by  an  alarm  system,  to  which  law enforcement is requested to respond.

Alarm system means any single device or assembly of  equipment designed to signal the occurrence of an illegal or unauthorized entry or other activity requiring immediate attention and to which law enforcement is requested to respond, including non-monitored alarms, but does not include motor vehicle or boat alarms, fire alarms, domestic violence alarms, or alarms designed to elicit a medical response.
Alarm user means any person, corporation, partnership, proprietorship, governmental or educational en-
tity or any other entity owning, leasing, or operating an alarm system, or on whose premises an alarm system is maintained for the protection of such premises.

Automatic dial protection device means an automatic dialing device or an automatic telephone dialing alarm system and shall include any system which, upon being activated, automatically initiates to the city police department a recorded message or code signal indicating a need for law enforcement response.

Cancellation means the process  where  response  is terminated  when  the  alarm  company  (designated  by the alarm user) notifies the city police department that there is not an existing situation at the alarm site requiring police response after an alarm dispatch request.
City means the City of Opa-locka or its agent.

False alarm means the activation of an alarm system through mechanical or electronic failure, malfunction, improper installation, or the negligence of  the alarm user, his/her employees or agents, and signals activated to summon law enforcement personnel unless law enforcement response was canceled by the alarm company before law enforcement personnel arrive at the alarm location. An alarm is false within the meaning of this  article  when,  upon  inspection  by  the  city  police department, evidence indicates that no unauthorized entry, robbery, or other such crime was committed or attempted  in  or  on  the  premises  which  would  have activated  a  properly  functioning  alarm  system.  Notwithstanding  the  foregoing,  a  false  alarm  shall  not include an alarm which can reasonably be determined to have been caused or activated by unusually violent conditions of nature, nor does it include other extraordinary circumstances not reasonably subject to control by the alarm user.
Permit year means a twelve (12) month period beginning  on  the  day  and  month  on  which  an  alarm permit is issued.

SIA Control Panel Standard CP-OI means the American National Standard Institute (ANSI) approved Security Industry Association (SIA) CP-Old Control Panel Standard as may be updated time to time that details recommended design features for security system control panels and their associated arming and disarming devices to reduce false alarms.
Verify means an attempt by the monitoring company,  or  its  representative  to  contact  the  alarm  site
POLICE

and/or alarm user by telephone and/or other electronic means, whether or not actual contact with a person is made to attempt to determine whether an alarm signal is valid before requesting law enforcement dispatch, in an  attempt  to  avoid  an  unnecessary  alarm  dispatch request.
Sec.  18-34.  Alarm permit.

(a) Permit required. No person shall use an alarm system monitored or non-monitored, without first obtaining a permit for such alarm system from the city police department. A fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) is  required  for  the  initial  registration  and  annual  renewal.  Alarm  permit  fee  amounts  may  be  amended from time to time by resolution of the city commission. Each alarm permit shall be assigned a unique permit number and the user shall provide the permit number to  the  alarm  company  to  facilitate  law  enforcement dispatch.

(b) Application. The permit shall be requested on an application  form  provided  by  the  city  police  department. An alarm user has the duty to obtain an application from the city police department.

Transfer of possession. When the possession of the premises at which an alarm system is maintained is transferred, the person (user) obtaining possession of the property shall file an application for an alarm permit within thirty (30) days of obtaining possession of  the property. Alarm permits are not transferable.

Reporting updated information. Whenever the information provided on the alarm permit application changes, the alarm user shall provide correct information to the city police department within ten (10) days of the change. In addition, each year after the issuance of  the permit, permit holders will receive from the city police department a form requesting updated information. The permit holder shall complete and return this form to the city police department when any of  the  requested  information  has changed; failure to comply will constitute a violation and may result in a civil penalty.
Multiple alarm systems. If an alarm user has one (1) or more alarm systems protecting two (2) or more
separate structures having different addresses and/or tenants, a separate permit shall be required for each structure and/or tenant.
Sec.  18-35.  Duties of the alarm user.
An alarm user must do the following:
Maintain the premises and the alarm system in a method that will reduce or eliminate false alarms.
Provide the alarm company the permit number (the number must be provided to the communications center by the alarm company to ensure dispatch).
Respond or cause a representative to respond to the alarm system's location within one (1) hour when notified by the city police department.
Not manually activate an alarm for any reason other than an occurrence of an event that the alarm system was intended to report.
Obtain a new permit and pay any associated fees if  there is a change in address or ownership of a business or residence.
It is the responsibility of  each alarm user to monitor the occurrences of false alarms on its premises.
Sec.  18-36.  Duties of the alarm company.
Any person engaged in the alarm business in the city, shall comply with the following:
Obtain and maintain the required state, county and/or city licenses.

Be  able  to  provide  name,  address,  and  telephone number of the alarm company license holder or a designee, who can be called in an emergency, twenty-four (24) hours a day; and be  able  to  respond  to  an  alarm  call,  when notified.
Be able to provide the most current contact information for the alarm user.
Ninety (90) days after enactment of this ordinance the alarm installation companies shall,
OPA-LOCKA CODE
on  all  new  and  upgraded  installations,  use only  alarm  control  panels  which  meet  SIA Control Panel Standard CP-O1.
Prior to activation of  the alarm system, the alarm company must provide instructions explaining  the  proper  operation  of  the  alarm system to the alarm user.
Provide written information of how to obtain service from the alarm company for the alarm system.
An alarm company performing monitoring services shall:

Attempt  to  verify,  by  calling  the  alarm  site and/or alarm user by telephone, to determine whether an alarm signal is valid before requesting dispatch. Telephone verification shall require,  as  a  minimum  that  a  second  call  be made to a different number, if the first attempt fails to reach an alarm user who can properly identify  themselves  to  attempt  to  determine whether an alarm signal is valid before requesting  law  enforcement  dispatch,  except  in  the case of a panic or robbery-in-progress alarm, or in cases where a crime-in-progress has been verified by video and/or audible means.
Provide alarm user registration number to the communications center to facilitate dispatch and/or cancellations.
Communicate any available information about the location of the alarm.
Communicate a cancellation to the law enforcement communications center as soon as possible following a determination that response is unnecessary.
Sec.  18-37.  Prohibited acts.

It shall be unlawful to activate an alarm system for the purpose of summoning law enforcement when no burglary, robbery, or other crime dangerous to life or property is being committed or attempted on the premises, or otherwise to cause a false alarm.
It shall be unlawful to install, maintain, or use an audible alarm system which can sound continually for more than fifteen (15) minutes.
It shall be unlawful to install, maintain, or use an automatic dial protection device that reports, or causes to be reported, any recorded message to the city police department.
Sec.  18-38.  Enforcement of provisions.

Excessive  false  alarms. It  is  hereby  found  and  determined  that  three  (3)  or  more  false  alarms  within  a permit year is excessive, constitutes a public nuisance, and shall be unlawful. Civil penalties for false alarms within a permit year shall be assessed against an alarm user as per current fee schedule.
Failure  to  register. It  shall  be  unlawful  to  operate  a burglar alarm system within the city without an alarm permit.
Other civil penalties. Violations will be enforced through the assessment of civil penalties.
Payment of civil penalties. Civil penalties shall be paid within thirty (30) days from the date of the invoice.
Civil non-criminal violation. A violation of  any of  the provisions of  this ordinance shall be a civil violation and shall not constitute a misdemeanor or infraction.
Discontinuance of law enforcement response. Police are not required to respond:
To burglar alarms at locations where six (6) or more false alarms occurred in the user's registration period.
To burglar alarms at locations where a burglar alarm civil penalty was not paid within thirty (30) days of a civil violation penalty notice.
To locations where the required alarm permit has not been obtained.

Notice of discontinuance of law enforcement response. A notice that police response will be discontinued, for any of  the above reasons, will accompany a civil violation notice, be posted at the affected locations, or be sent to the user by certified mail at least thirty (30) days prior to discontinuing service.
POLICE
Restoring  police  response  to  terminated  locations. To regain police response to burglar alarms at terminated locations, the alarm user must:

Pay all outstanding burglar alarm civil penalties.
Apply for and obtain an alarm permit. (Code 1983, § 18-38; Ord. No. 2021-03, § 1, 1-13-2021)

Alarm registration  is  not  intended  to,  nor  will  it, create a contract, duty or obligation, either expressed or implied, of response. ARTICLE III.  GATED COMMUNITIES
Sec.  18-46.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Fire inspector means the office or person designated as the fire inspector to provide services on behalf of the city, otherwise consistent with this Code.

Gate means a gate, crossbar, door, or other obstructive device which is utilized for the purpose of restricting, controlling, or obstructing entry or exit by motor vehicles or pedestrians to or from a private roadway.
Gates community/gated community means a development, whether single-family, multifamily, commercial, industrial, or accessory use, that is enclosed within a geographical area by restrictive gates.
OPA-LOCKA CODE
Key pad means a secure, tamperproof device operable for the provision of police and fire services. (Code 1983, § 18-46; Ord. No. 08-09, § 2, 9-10-2008)
Sec.  18-47.  Intent.

The intent of this article is to require key pad access to gated communities for the provision of  police and fire accessibility in emergency situations. (Code 1983, § 18-47; Ord. No. 08-09, § 2, 9-10-2008)
Sec.  18-48.  Requirements.
Access gate key boxes for gated communities shall be of the types approved by the city and shall:
(1) Require a permit to be issued by the department of planning and zoning or a fire inspector showing approval. Permits shall be kept on file within said department.
(2) Provide a key pad entry system that shall be installed in an accessible location and provide for a coded number designated by the police chief for police and fire service entry.
(3) Access gates must be designed to provide automatic entry for fire apparatus in the form of siren  activation,  scanners  or  other  approved methods.
(4) All access gates shall be designated to unlock with a readily accessible manual releasing device.
(5) During power failure, all access gates shall be designated to fail in the open position.
(6) A key box shall be installed at the gate in all gated communities.
Sec.  18-49.  Maintenance.

The key pads shall be kept in working order and shall  be  repaired  and  replaced  in  the  event  they  are damaged or disabled. Proper maintenance of  the key pad shall solely be the responsibility of  the property owner.
Sec.  18-50.  Violations.
The following are violations and penalties of  this article:

(1) If  it  is  found  that  a  gated  community  is  in violation of  this article, the property owners shall be contacted in writing by the city manager and required to remedy the violation immediately.

(2) Any violations that have remained after seven (7)  business  days  will  be  fined  for  everyday thereafter. Fines will be assessed at one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) per day until the violation has been corrected. After fifteen (15) days of  noncompliance, the fine will increase incrementally  fifty  dollars  ($50.00)  per  day until the violation has been corrected up to the legal limit.

Sec.  19-1.  Official map.

(a) Adopted. Pursuant to the provisions, restrictions and limitations of section 2.5(8) of the Charter of the city, the map, identified as Exhibit A, attached to Ordinance No. 320 and by reference thereto made a part hereof, is adopted and established as the official map of the city.

(b) Intent; modifications. Any construction of  the commission's intent in the adoption of this section and the establishment of said official map shall be consistent with the provisions of said section 2.5(8). (Code 1955, §§ 2-7.3, 2-7.4; Code 1983, § 19-1)
Sec.  19-2.  Structures on mapped streets.
(a) Prohibited. No permit shall  be  issued  for  any building or structure or any part thereof  on any land located between the mapped lines of a street as shown on the official map.

(b) Exceptions. The planning and zoning board shall have and is hereby given the power, upon an appeal filed with it by the owner of land, to grant a permit, for a building or structure or part thereof in any mapped street location in any case in which said board finds, upon the evidence and arguments presented to it upon appeal:
(a) That the entire property of  the appellant of which a mapped street location forms a part, cannot yield a reasonable return to the owner unless such permit is granted; and

(b) That, balancing the interest of the city in preserving the integrity of  the official map and the interest of the owner of the property in the use and benefits of  his property, the grant of such permit is required by considerations of reasonable justice and equity.
Sec.  19-3.  Work  to  comply  with  state  standards  and specifications.

All construction, repair or other work done upon any street, sidewalk or public way shall comply in all respects with the standards and specifications of  the state  department  of  transportation  for  similar  work done on state roads. (Code 1983, § 19-3)
Sec.  19-4.  Obstructions generally.

No person shall place any trash, lumber, wood, glass or other obstruction in any public street, lane, alley or way, or on any sidewalk. Any person who shall place any obstruction as aforesaid in any sidewalk and fail to remove the same within six (6) hours after being notified by the chief of police or any police officer, or who, after having removed the obstruction, shall replace it or place similar obstructions, shall be guilty of a violation of this Code.

It  shall  be  unlawful  to  permit  shrubbery  or  any growth to grow upon or to maintain the same upon any parcel of land at the intersection of any public ways in the city so that the same will obstruct the view of  the driver  or  operator  of  any  vehicle  approaching  such intersection.
Sec.  19-6.  Street sales.

It shall be unlawful to sell, offer to sell or exhibit for sale, any goods, wares or merchandise from any parked vehicle  or  stand  set  up  upon  any  street  in  the  city; provided, however, that this prohibition shall not be applicable to public markets or to peddlers operating under  a  city  permit  when  the  rules  and  regulations governing the issuance of such permit shall have been complied with.

Sec.  19-9.  School zone speed limits.

A. Purpose. The implementation of speed detection systems affixed on select roads that are maintained as school zones within the city promotes the safety of the city  residents,  Miami-Dade  County  School  District employees, and grade school children seeking an education within the city. The automated system will capture evidence of drivers in violation of this article and F.S.  §  316.1896,  thus,  promoting  adherence  and  safe driving practices within proper designated school zones.

B. Intent. This article authorizes the city, in accordance with chapter 2023-174 Laws of Florida and F.S. §  316.008,  as  amended,  to  exercise  its  authority  in placing and installing speed detection systems in various  school  zones  with  the  boundaries  of  the  city's jurisdiction. The placement and installation of  speed detection systems on roads maintained as school zone will allow the city to identify violations of  this article
and  F.S.  §  316.1896,  enforce  the  provisions  of  this ordinance, and promote the safety of student and parent welfare.

C. Use of speed detection systems. This article shall not supersede, infringe, curtail or impinge upon state or county laws related to school zone speed limit violations  or  conflict  with  such  laws.  This  article  shall serve to enable the city to provide enhanced enforcement within school zones pursuant to Florida Statutes. The city shall utilize speed detection systems to deter school zone speed limit infractions and to thereby reduce accidents and injuries authorized to employ the services of a third party vendor for purposes of implementing this article.
D. Speed detection system enforcement; signage; violation.

(a) Pursuant to F.S. § 316.0776, as amended, the city shall post signage indicating that the subject school zone is subject to photographic and video enforcement of  the school zone speed limit and notify the public of the specific times of enforcement.
(b) Pursuant to F.S. § 316.1896, as amended, the owner of  a motor vehicle violates this article and state law when the operator of such vehicle:

1. Operates a motor vehicle in excess of ten (10) miles per hour over the school zone speed  limit  which  occurs  within  thirty (30) minutes before through thirty (30) minutes  after  the  start  of  a  regularly scheduled breakfast program;

2. Operates a motor vehicle in excess of ten (10) miles per hour over the school zone speed  limit  which  occurs  within  thirty (30) minutes before through thirty (30) minutes  after  the  start  of  a  regularly scheduled school session;
3. Operates a motor vehicle in excess of ten (10) miles per hour over the posted speed limit during the entirety of  a regularly scheduled school session; or
4. Operates a motor vehicle in excess of ten (10) miles per hour over the school zone speed  limit  which  occurs  within  thirty
OPA-LOCKA CODE
(30) minutes before through thirty (30) minutes after the end of a regularly scheduled school session.

(c) A  violation  of  this  article  occurs  when  the operator  of  a  motor  vehicle  fails  to  comply with requirements of  subsection D(b) of  this section. Violations shall be enforced pursuant to F.S. § 316.1896.
E. Review of  recorded photographic and video evidence.

(a) The owner of the vehicle which is observed by recorded images operating a motor vehicle in violation  of  applicable  city  law)  and  F.S. § 316.1896, shall be issued a notice of violation in accordance with state law.

(b) A law enforcement officer and/or designated a traffic infraction enforcement officer shall review recorded images prior to the issuance of a notice of  violation/infraction to ensure accuracy and the integrity of the recorded images. Once the officer has verified the accuracy of the  recorded  images  a  notice  of  violation/ infraction shall be sent to the vehicle owner at the address on record with the state department of highway safety and motor vehicles or the  address  on  record  with  the  appropriate agency  having  such  information  in  another state.

(c) A speed detection system in a school zone may not be used for remote surveillance. The collection of  evidence by a speed detection system to enforce violations of  this  article  and F.S. § 316.1895 and 316.183, or user-controlled pan or tilt adjustments of speed detection system components, do not constitute remote surveillance.

1. Any recorded video or photograph obtained through the use of a speed detection  system  must  be  destroyed  within ninety (90) days after the final disposition of  the recorded event. The vendor of  a  speed  detection  system  must  provide the county or municipality with written notice by December 31 of each year that such records have been destroyed in accordance with this subsection.

2. Registered motor vehicle owner information obtained as a result of the operation of  a speed detection system in a school zone is not the property of the manufacturer or vendor of  the speed detection system  and  may  be  used  only  for  the purposes of this article.
F. Notice of violation and affidavits.

(a) Within thirty (30) days after a violation, notice must be sent  to  the  registered  owner  of  the motor vehicle involved in the violation specifying the remedies available and that the violator must pay the penalty to the city or furnish an affidavit within thirty (30) days after the date of the notice of violation in order to avoid court fees, costs, and the issuance of  a uniform traffic citation. The notice of  violation must:
1. Be sent by first class mail.

2. Include a photograph or other recorded image showing the license plate of  the motor vehicle; the date, time, and location of the violation; the maximum speed at which the motor vehicle was traveling within  the  school  zone;  and  the  speed limit within the school zone at the time of the violation.

3. Include a notice that the owner has the right  to  review,  in  person  or  remotely, the photograph or video captured by the speed detection system and the evidence of  the  speed  of  the  motor  vehicle  detected  by  the  speed  detection  system which constitute a rebuttable presumption that the motor vehicle was used in violation of this article and F .S. § 316.1895 or 316.183.
4. State  the  time  when,  and  the  place  or website at which, the photograph or video captured,  and  evidence  of  speed  detected may be examined and observed.

(b) A person who receives a notice of  violation under this section may request a hearing within thirty (30) days after the notice of violation or may pay the penalty pursuant to the notice of violation,  but  a  payment  or  fee  may  not  be required before the hearing requested by the

ARTICLE II.  SIDEWALK CONSTRUCTION AND REPAIR*
Sec.  19-18.  Construction prerequisite to building permit or certificate of occupancy.

No permit for the construction of  any building on any lot or parcel of land within the city, whether platted or unplatted, except within industrially zoned districts, shall be issued unless the plans and specifications shall include as part of the entire construction sidewalks in accordance with standard specifications prepared by the department of public works and utilities. No certificate of occupancy shall be issued until completion and approval  of  the  construction  of  sidewalks  required hereunder. The city manager may waive construction of  sidewalks  on  the  grounds  set  forth  for  waiver  of plats, subject to confirmation by the city commission.
Sec.  19-19.  Establishment, marking of lines and grades.

Requirements for lines and grades for the building of sidewalks shall be furnished by the city. The contractor shall furnish all stakes or pins and such ordinary labor as may be necessary for setting grades. He shall also take necessary steps to protect and care for the stakes after grade is set, and if any one (1) of the stakes is disturbed the grade shall be reset at the contractor's expense.
Sec.  19-20.  Permit required.
It shall be unlawful to construct or install any sidewalk upon or along any public way in the city without having first obtained a permit therefor from the director of public works.
Sec.  19-21.  Fees for permits.
The fees for sidewalk permits within the city are as presently established or as hereafter adopted by resolution of the city commission.

Sec.  19-22.  Notice prior to beginning work.

After grades are finished, at least twenty-four (24) hours' notice shall be given the city by the contractor before actual construction of a sidewalk is begun, the contractor specifying as nearly as practicable, the hour at which he expects to start work. The fact that a permit has been secured or grades given shall not constitute legal notice.
Sec.  19-23.  Material and specifications.

All  sidewalks  constructed  within  the  official  base building and street lines in the city shall be constructed only of natural uncolored Portland cement concrete, in accordance with the city standards and specification. (Code 1955, § 19-29; Code 1983, § 19-23)
Sec.  19-24.  Dangerous prohibited.

It shall be unlawful for any owner or occupant, or agent thereof, of  any property to which a sidewalk is contiguous to allow such walk or sidewalk to remain in such a condition as to be dangerous or detrimental to the public.
Sec.  19-25.  Duty to repair; notice.

In case the surface of  any walk or sidewalk in the city shall become so uneven as to make walking over it dangerous or detrimental, or if  the curbing shall become decayed, worn out or broken, it shall become the duty, upon notice to the owner, and if the owner cannot be served, to the occupant, and if there is no occupant, then the agent of the owner of the property, to which the  sidewalk  is  contiguous,  to  repair  such  walk  or sidewalk. Such notice shall be in writing and allow such owner, agent or occupant thirty (30) days in which to repair such walk or sidewalk; shall describe the walk, sidewalk or curb to be repaired and shall set forth that such walk, sidewalk or curb is to be repaired, if surface work is to be done, with the same material as such walk, sidewalk  or  curb  was  originally  constructed;  and  if curbing is to be put in, shall state that it will be concrete.

ARTICLE III.  NAMING OF PUBLIC FACILITIES AND STREETS
Sec.  19-26.  Naming and renaming procedure of facilities and streets.

After the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived, no public facility or street located in  or  owned  by  the  city  shall  be  named  or  renamed except in accordance with the procedures set forth in this article.
Sec.  19-27.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
(a) Reserved.

(b) Committee means the street naming committee and shall also mean the city commission or any other such committee designated by the city  commission  to  review  and  recommend names for public facilities and streets located within or owned by the city.

(c) Main  street means  one  (1)  of  the  following roadways located in the city: Sharazad Boulevard, Opa-locka Boulevard, Ali-Baba Avenue, Perviz  Avenue,  Oriental  Boulevard,  Aswan Road and Alexandria Drive.
(d) Plaza means an open public square.
(e) Public facility means any public building, plaza or park owned by the city.
Sec.  19-28.  Review  and  recommendation  by  commission.

The commission shall consider the selection criteria set forth in subsection (c) of  this section which, when approved by the city commission, shall govern its name selection process and/or dual designation process.
Whenever a name is needed for a new public facility or street or whenever there is a proposal to rename an existing public facility or street within or owned by the

city, said naming or renaming shall first be considered and reviewed by the city commission according to the following procedures:

(a) Any person, organization, association, corporation or other entity including a member of the city commission or the administration of the city may propose a name for a new public facility owned by the city or city street or may propose renaming an existing public facility or city street at any time by submitting a proposal in the form of an ordinance.

(b) Prior  to  a  final  vote  on  the  item  and  after presentation of the ordinance of said proposal the  commission  shall  meet  to  consider  and review proposals for the naming or renaming of  said public facility or street. There shall also be a discussion that one (1) or more of  the following minimum criteria can be established prior to passage of any proposal for the renaming of a public facility or street:

ARTICLE IV.  REQUIREMENT TO NUMBER ALL BUILDINGS
Sec.  19-35.  General intent and applicability.

It is the intent of this article to promote, protect and improve the safety, services and welfare of the citizens of the city by providing a requirement that all buildings be affixed with numbers in conformity with these provisions. Such a requirement will:
(1) Ensure greater public safety;
(2) Promote  efficiency  in  the  postal  and  other delivery services; and
(3) Improve the emergency call-response system for medical, fire and police services.
The requirements of  this article shall apply to all buildings within the city.
STREETS AND SIDEWALKS
Sec.  19-36.  Numbers to comply with article; authority of department of building and licensing.
The  numbering  of  all  buildings  within  the  city's limits shall be in conformity with the following system:
(a) All  numbering  of  number  units  shall  begin from  the  base  thoroughfare;  the  north  and east sides of  the streets having the odd numbers and the south and west having the even numbers.
(b) The numbers of each number unit in a square shall  increase  in  arithmetical  progression  of two (2) as the number units recede from the base thoroughfare.

(c) The  director  of  the  department  of  building and licensing and the director of  the department of  planning and zoning are hereby directed to designate the building numbers, including single-family houses, apartment buildings and other multi-unit buildings, and commercial  buildings,  as  herein  provided,  if necessary.

(d) All  buildings,  houses,  portions  of  land  and lots  adjacent  to  or  abutting  (joining  end  to end)  upon  streets,  avenues,  places,  terraces, courts,  lanes  and  roads  of  the  city  shall  be known and designated by the numbers indicated on the appropriate plats as retained by the city's department of buildings and licensing and the department of planning and community development.
Sec.  19-37.  Building numbers specifications.
Numbers on buildings shall conform to the following specifications:

(a) The numbers shall have a minimum height of four  (4)  inches.  It  is  recommended  that  the height of  the numbers exceed four (4) inches. Examples  of  numbers  measuring  four  (4) inches,  five  (5)  inches  and  six  (6)  inches  in height are attached to the ordinance from which this section is derived.
(b) All numbers shall be securely mounted on the building front, or any fixed accessory located in front of  the building within five (5) feet of the  main  entry  way  or  main  path  of  travel

which leads to the main entrance of the building from a public or private road. Such numbers shall otherwise be separately mounted in the same manner upon the face of  a wall or fence or upon a post in the front yard of  the property.

(c) Numbers shall be sufficiently legible as to contrasting background, arrangement, size, spacing, and uniformity of  numerals, so that the numbers may be read with ease during daylight  hours  by  a  person  possessing  at  least 20/40 vision upon viewing said numbers from the center line of the adjacent road. The numbers  shall  be  placed  such  that  trees,  shrubs, and other obstructions do not block the line of sight of the numbers from the centerline of the adjacent road.

(d) Wherever practicable and in accordance with this article, the building numbers shall be placed as close as possible to a light source, in order to make it more visible at night. If no light source is  close  in  proximity,  the  numbers  shall  be made of a reflective material.
Sec.  19-38.  Duty of owners of buildings.

(a)  It shall be the duty of the owner of any building facing, abutting, opening or having its main entrance from any right-of-way in the city to have affixed to such building suitable numbers composed of figures no less than four (4) inches in height, and/or upon panel glass or  some  metallic  substance,  in  accordance  with  the plats of the city.

(b)  It  shall  be  the  duty  of  the  owner  to  maintain numbers  of  his  building  as  herein  required  in  good condition and in a conspicuous place where same can be seen and read from the street, in accordance with the requirements of this article.
(c)  It shall be the duty of  the owner to check with the department of buildings and licensing to ascertain his correct address if he is uncertain of it.
(d)  The word "owner," as used in this article, shall include owners of the real property, a lessee and agent in charge.

ARTICLE I.  IN GENERAL
Sec.  19.5-1.  Additional  homestead  tax  exemption  for certain persons 65 years of age and older.
For purposes of this section, the terms "household" and "household income" shall have the same meanings as ascribed to them in F .S. § 196.075, as may be amended from time to time.

In accordance with section 6(d), article VII of  the Florida Constitution and F.S. § 196.075, any person sixty-five (65) years or over who has legal or equitable title to real estate located within the city and maintains thereon  his/her  permanent  residence  which  qualifies for and receives a homestead exemption pursuant to section 6(a), article VII of  the Florida Constitution, and whose household income does not exceed the greater of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000.00) or the income limitation amount adjusted in 2007 pursuant to F.S. § 196.075(3), shall be entitled to make application for an additional homestead exemption of up to fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00).

Every person claiming the additional exemption pursuant to this section must file annually an application ("application") and supporting documentation ("documentation") with the county property appraiser ("property appraiser"), not later than March 1 of  each year for  which  the  additional  exemption  is  claimed.  The application shall include a sworn statement of  household  income  for  all  members  of  the  household  and shall be filed on a firm prescribed by the state department of revenue. The documentation shall include copies of all federal income tax returns, wage and earnings statements, any requests for extension of time to file a return, and any other documentation as required by the property appraiser, including documentation necessary to verify the income received by all of the members of the household for the prior year.
Failure to file the application, documentation and sworn statement by March 1 of  any given year shall constitute a waiver of the additional exemption privilege for that year.

The additional  exemption  shall  be  available  commencing with the year 2007 tax roll, and the property appraiser may begin accepting applications and sworn statements  for  the  year  2007  tax  roll  as  soon  as  the appropriate forms are available from the department of revenue.

Commencing January 1, 2007, and each January 1 thereafter, the twenty thousand dollar ($20,000.00) annual income limitation in this section shall be adjusted by  the  percentage  of  change  in  the  average  cost-ofliving index for the calendar year immediately prior to that year. The term "index" shall be the average of the monthly  consumer-price  index  figures  for  the  stated period, for the United States as a whole, issued by the United States Department of Labor.
Sec.  19.5-2.  Additional  tax  exemption  for  certain  senior citizens.
(a)  Pursuant  to  Fla.  Const.  art.  VII,  §  6(d)m,  a homestead exemption from municipal taxes levied by the city equal to the assessed value of  the property is hereby granted if:
(1) The fair market value of  the property is less than  two  hundred  fifty  thousand  dollars ($250,000.00);
(2) The owner has been a permanent resident on the property for at least 25 years; and
(3) The property owner is at least 65 years of age and  has  a  household  income  that  does  not exceed the maximum amount established for this exemption.

(b)  A taxpayer claiming the exemption for the first time submit to the county property appraiser, not later than March 1, a sworn statement of household income on a form prescribed by the state department of revenue.

ARTICLE II.  UTILITY TAX*
Sec.  19.5-21.  Short title.
This  article  shall  be  known  as  the  "City  of  Opalocka Public Service Tax Ordinance."
*State law referencePublic service tax, F.S. §§ 166.231, 166.232.
OPA-LOCKA CODE
Sec.  19.5-22.  Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

Bottled gas means all types and kinds of  natural, liquefied petroleum and manufactured gas for lighting, heating, cooking, power, or any other purpose delivered to any purchaser thereof within the city.
Coal or other fossil fuels means all combustible fossil fuels not otherwise exempt by law from taxation.
Electricity means all electric current or energy for lighting, heating, cooking, power, or any other purpose delivered to any purchaser thereof within the city.

Fuel  adjustment  charge means  all  increases  in  the cost of utility services to the ultimate customer resulting  from  increase  in  the  cost  of  fuel  to  the  utility subsequent to October 1, 1973.

Fuel oil means all petroleum fuels including bunker C oil, Number 1 and Number 2 fuel oil, and kerosene or any combination thereof for lighting, heating, cooking, power, or any other purpose delivered to any purchaser thereof within the city.
Metered gas means all types and kinds of  natural and manufactured gas for lighting, heating, cooking, power, or any other purpose delivered to any purchaser thereof within the city.

Purchase means every act  or  transaction  whereby possession  of,  utilization  of,  control  over  or  title  to electricity, water, metered gas, bottled gas, and fuel oil, and the duty and obligation to pay therefor, become vested in the purchaser within the city, but such term shall not pertain to nor include any such act or transaction when undertaken or performed by an agency or instrumentality of  the United States government, the state, the county, or a municipality.

Purchaser means every person legally liable for the payment of electricity, metered gas, bottled gas, or fuel oil  delivery  rendered  to  him,  by  a  seller,  unless  such person is an agency or instrumentality of  the United States government, the state, the county, a municipality, or a house of  public worship, which qualified for exemption from the state sales tax under F.S. § 212.08.
Seller means every person delivering electricity, metered  gas,  bottled  gas,  or  fuel  oil,  to  any  purchaser thereof.

Taxable  services means  services  subject  to  public service tax are electricity, metered or bottled gas (natural liquefied petroleum gas or manufactured), coal or fossil fuels and competitive services.
Sec.  19.5-23.  Determination of amount.

There is hereby levied and imposed by the city upon every  purchase  in  the  city  of  electricity,  metered  or bottled gas (natural liquefied petroleum gas or manufactured), coal or fossil fuels and competitive services known as "taxable services" included in or reflected by any bill rendered by the seller to the purchaser a public service tax which shall be determined as follows:

(1) The tax shall be levied only upon purchases within the city. The tax shall not exceed ten (10) percent of  the payments received by the seller of  the taxable item from the purchaser for the purchase of such service. Services competitive with those enumerated above shall be taxed on a comparable base at the same rates. However, fuel oil shall be taxed at a rate not to exceed four cents ($0.04) per gallon.

(2) When the seller in accordance with its rules and regulations renders a bill to the purchaser to cover purchases made during the period of time to which the bill is applicable, the amount of public service tax shall be exclusive of governmental  charges  and  taxes,  shown  on  any such bill due and payable on account of such purchases, for the total amount; provided, however,  that  the  portion  of  the  utility  bill  that represents a surcharge or adjustment caused by  increased  cost  of  energy-producing  fuels shall be exempt from taxation and no tax shall be levied or imposed thereon.

(3) Purchases of taxable services shall be considered  and  treated  as  constituting  and  being distinct  and  unrelated  classes  of  purchases, and in the event that more than one (1) such class shall be shown upon the same bill, the amount of public utility tax payable pursuant hereto shall be determined and computed for each such class separately.

(4) The seller is required and it shall be his duty to render to each purchaser bills covering all such purchases made, and the amount of such public utility tax shall be entered and shown by the seller as a separate item on each such bill and shall become due and payable to the city whenever such bill becomes due and payable under the  rules  and  regulations  of  the  seller.  Each such bill shall include purchases applicable to but one (1) location, or to but one (1) family or business  where  more  than  one  (1)  family  or business uses separate metered services at one (1) location in the city.

(5) The purchaser is required and it shall be his duty to pay such public utility tax to the seller, as agent for the city, at the time of the payment of  each  such  bill,  and  in  the  event  that  the purchaser shall fail, neglect or refuse to pay such public utility tax to the seller when such bill  becomes  due  and  payable,  the  seller  is hereby empowered to discontinue forthwith to make any further sales or to render any further service to the purchaser until the total amount, including such public utility tax, shown upon such  bill  has  been  paid  in  full.  The  seller  is hereby authorized and required and it shall be his duty to collect such public utility tax from such purchaser at the time of the payment of each  such  bill  and  to  remit  the  same  to  the department of finance in accordance with the provisions hereinafter stated, provided that the seller shall have the right and privilege of  assuming and paying such excise tax himself in lieu of collecting the same from the purchaser; and that whenever the seller shall fail or neglect to collect such public utility tax from the purchaser within one (1) year from the date of the bill on which such tax was or should have been imposed, the seller  shall  be  deemed  to have assumed such public utility tax himself and shall thereupon become liable for the payment of the amount thereof to the city to the same extent as if  such public utility tax has been  collected  from  the  purchaser,  without further recourse to the purchaser therefor.
(6) This section shall be applicable to all bills for taxable services, except that any bills for the purchase of sixteen (16) ounces or less of bot-
tled  gas  in  a  container  or  less  than  one  (1) gallon of  fuel oil shall be exempt from taxation.
Sec.  19.5-24.  Exemptions.
Exempt from taxation are the following:

(1) The first five hundred (500) kilowatt hours of electricity purchased per month for residential use. This exemption shall apply to each separate residential unit regardless of whether such unit is  on  a  separate  or  a  central  meter  and shall be passed on to each individual tenant by the  seller.  In  addition,  the  exemption  shall include customer service charges, franchise fees, and all other costs, fees, or charges insofar as the same relate to the first five hundred (500) kilowatt hours.

(2) Natural gas or fuel oil purchased by a public or private utility, either for resale or for use as fuel  in  the  generation  of  electricity,  or  the purchase of fuel oil or kerosene for the use as an aircraft engine fuel or propellant or for use in  internal  combustion  engines  shall  be  exempt from taxation hereunder.
(3) Purchases  by  any  recognized  church  in  this state for use exclusively for church purposes.
(4) Services  competitive  with  those  enumerated above shall be taxed on a comparable base at the same rates. However, fuel oil shall be taxed at a rate not to exceed four cents ($0.04) per gallon.
Sec.  19.5-24.1.  Enterprise zone; partial utility tax exemption.

(a)  Pursuant to F.S. § 166.231(8), the city grants an exemption of  fifty (50) percent of  the municipal tax imposed for purchases of electrical energy on purchasers of electrical energy who are determined by the state department of revenue, pursuant to F.S. § 212.08(15), to  be  a  qualified  business  at  a  fixed  location  in  an enterprise zone.
(b)  The  exemption  provided  in  subsection  (a)  of this section shall be available to any business which is new or substantially expanded.

(c)  The exemption provided in subsection (a) of this section shall be available for all businesses determined qualified as provided in subsection (a) of  this section for five (5) years from the date of such determination, provided that no business shall be deemed qualified for the exemption after December 31, 1994.

(d)  This section shall expire and be void on December 31, 1984, except that any qualified business which has satisfied the requirements of  this section prior to December 31, 1994, shall be allowed the full benefit of the  exemption  allowed  under  this  section  as  if  this section had not yet expired on December 31, 1994.
Sec.  19.5-25.  Remittance to the city by seller.

Every seller is hereby required to execute and file not later than the twentieth day of each month at the office of the department of finance a certified statement on a form prescribed by such department, setting forth the amount  of  such  public  utility  tax  to  which  the  city became  entitled  under  the  provisions  hereof  on  account of bills paid by purchasers during the preceding fiscal month, and contemporaneously with the filing of such statements, shall pay the amount of  such public utility  tax  to  the  department  of  finance.  Failure  to timely remit the tax shall obligate the seller to pay to the city a penalty of one (1) percent thereof per month or fraction thereof during the period of delinquency. All collected tax and penalties shall be deposited to credit of the general fund of the city to be expended for city purposes.
Sec.  19.5-26.  Records to be kept.

Every seller is hereby required to establish and maintain appropriate accounts and records showing in such detail as the director of  the finance department may prescribe the amount of such public utility tax payable to the city under the provisions hereof  and such accounts and records shall be open to inspection by the finance  director  or  his  duly  authorized  agent  at  all reasonable times. The director of  the finance department is hereby authorized and empowered to promulgate from time to time such rules and regulations with respect to the establishment and maintenance of such
accounts  and  records  as  he  may  deem  necessary  to carry into effect the purpose and intent of  the provisions hereof.
Sec.  19.5-27.  Reports of deliveries for resale.

Every manufacturer, distributor, wholesaler or seller who shall deliver taxable services to any seller or other person having a place of business in the city, or licensed to do business therein, to be sold or resold to ultimate purchasers, shall report to the department of  finance semiannually,  as  of  June  30  and  December  31,  the names and addresses of such sellers or other persons, and the quantities received by each of them during the preceding six (6) months, such reports to be filed not later than one (1) month after the close of each semiannual period.
